articles.title: Defesa Civil envia aviso após 'calor acima do normal' em Fortaleza | G1
articles.standfirst: Conforme o órgão, capital cearense tem registrado sensação térmica em torno dos 39ºC durante os últimos dias, além de noites com sensação de até 30ºC.
articles.summary: Conforme o órgão, capital cearense tem registrado sensação térmica em torno dos 39ºC durante os últimos dias, além de noites com sensação de até 30ºC.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Moradores de Fortaleza receberam uma mensagem da Defesa Civil , na tarde desta quarta-feira (25), com orientações para a população em uma semana de “calor acima do normal”. O aviso preventivo foi enviado após o monitoramento da sensação térmica na capital cearense.

“Fortaleza registra semana de calor acima do normal. Beba água, busque sombra e redobre o cuidado com crianças, idosos e pets” , diz a mensagem enviada por SMS para números cadastrados para receber alertas (confira abaixo na reportagem como fazer o cadastro) .

De acordo com o coronel Haroldo Gondim, coordenador da Defesa Civil de Fortaleza, a mensagem foi enviada após a persistência do calor mais intenso por quatro dias na capital.

🌡️ Segundo o órgão, Fortaleza teve as quatro últimas noites com temperaturas a partir dos 28ºC e sensação térmica de até 30ºC . Durante o dia, o coordenador explica que a sensação térmica média registrada tem sido de aproximadamente 39ºC .

Moradores de Fortaleza recebem aviso da Defesa Civil após dias de sensações térmicas elevadas — Foto: Reprodução

O coordenador do órgão explica que a sensação térmica tem variações de acordo com as condições do lugar onde cada pessoa se encontra.

“Isso ainda pode ser majorado se, de repente, você mora em uma região mais adensada, com construção sem janelas, que tem obstáculos, e o vento não chega, que tem menos cobertura vegetal, mais asfalto… Tudo isso vai sendo condicionante para que essa situação ainda possa ser piorada”, contextualiza.

Este acompanhamento é realizado com auxílio de 20 estações meteorológicas instaladas em regiões da cidade , alcançando uma cobertura de 70% da área do município.

Os dados gerados, que incluem temperatura, sensação térmica e umidade, podem ser acompanhados em tempo real no Observatório de Riscos Climáticos , lançado pela Prefeitura de Fortaleza.

Conforme o coronel Haroldo Gondim, a Defesa Civil está em articulação com outros órgãos e instituições, como as pastas de saúde, educação e proteção social, para monitorar um possível aumento de demanda nos serviços e atendimentos que indiquem efeitos do calor intenso na população.

Ele explica que, até o momento, não houve a identificação de problemas maiores reportados em Fortaleza.

Cuidados em dias de sensação térmica elevada incluem beber água e diminuir exposição prolongada ao sol — Foto: Shutterstock

As orientações para reforçar a hidratação e evitar situações que prolonguem a exposição ao calor são válidas para toda a população diante de sensações térmicas elevadas associadas ao fenômeno El Niño 2026-2027.

➡️ O cenário exige atenção especial para alguns grupos que podem ficar mais vulneráveis . Dentre eles, estão:

Pessoas com comorbidades e problemas cardiovasculares

“Estas pessoas têm que procurar beber água, pelo menos a cada duas horas, usar roupas leves, usar filtro solar, se proteger. Se tiver algum compromisso em áreas externas que possa ser adiado, adiar nesse momento, procurar estar em ambientes mais frescos, mais ventilados e sombreados, pois isso ameniza bastante essa sensação de calor”, orienta o coordenador.

⚠️ A população também deve ficar atenta aos sintomas de desidratação e mal-estar associado ao calor extremo, como tontura, fraqueza e dor de cabeça .

🚨 Em casos graves, como desmaios ou alterações da consciência , a orientação é procurar atendimento de urgência.

Os alertas da Defesa Civil podem ser recebidos para quem se cadastrar por SMS. Para isso, basta enviar uma mensagem com o número do CEP da área de interesse para o número 40199 .

Outra opção é se cadastrar para receber atualizações da Defesa Civil Nacional pelo WhatsApp, cadastrando o número (61) 2034.4611 e enviando uma mensagem.

articles.title: EUA fazem explosão controlada de material tóxico  | G1
articles.standfirst: Quase 70 barris de azida de chumbo foram detonados nesta quarta-feira (25), no estado de Iowa. Operação chegou a ser adiada três vezes, por temores a danos ambientais e para moradores, mas recebeu autorização da Justiça. Trump disse que análise inicial indicou que não houve impacto.
articles.summary: O Exército dos Estados Unidos realizou a polêmica explosão controlada de 68 barris de azida de chumbo, substância usada na fabricação de munições, após autorização da Justiça.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O Exército dos Estados Unidos realizou nesta quarta-feira (25) a polêmica explosão controlada de 68 barris de azida de chumbo, substância usada na fabricação de munições.

A detonação ocorreu no estado de Iowa e só foi possível com autorização da Justiça, após uma disputa envolvendo possíveis riscos à saúde dos moradores locais e ao meio ambiente (leia mais abaixo) .

O presidente dos EUA, Donald Trump , disse que análises iniciais indicaram que esforços para "mitigar danos" foram bem sucedidos . No início da semana, o líder norte-americano se opôs à detonação.

O governador de Missouri, estado vizinho a Iowa, disse que uma "análise inicial" indicou que não houve imprevistos .

"A análise inicial compartilhada conosco por parceiros federais e pela Segurança Interna e Gerenciamento de Emergências de Iowa indica que as medidas de mitigação parecem ter sido bem-sucedidas e a explosão foi bem contida", disse o governador Mike Kehoe.

Nuvel de fumaça é vista no local onde Exército dos EUA detonou material explosivo, em Middletown, Iowa, em 25 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Jim Urquhart/ Reuters

Vestidos com equipamento especial, jornalistas esperam detonação controlada de explosivos pelo Exército dos Estados Unidos em Iowa, em 25 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Jim Urquhart/ Reuters

Transmissões ao vivo das agências de notícias mostraram, ao longe, uma coluna de fumaça subindo no local após estrondos causados pela detonação (veja no vídeo acima) . Em Middletown, cidade próxima do local onde ocorreu a detonação, no estado de Iowa, moradores ouviram barulhos de duas fortes explosões em sequência.

O Exército dos EUA, encarregado do procedimento, ainda não havia se pronunciado após a detonação até a última atualização desta reportagem.

Mais cedo, o Exército divulgou um vídeo mostrando os preparativos para a explosão. Uma estrutura com bancos de areia e galões de água foi construída ao redor do material radioativo para acomodar a detonação.

"Militares trabalham ininterruptamente para minimizar os impactos da detonação controlada. As medidas incluem uma barreira de água com mais de 379 mil litros, barreiras de contenção de terra, blocos preenchidos com areia, modelagem especializada da dispersão de materiais e lonas para controle de temperatura", afirmou o Exército em comunicado nas redes sociais.

Soldados foram de casa em casa entre terça e quarta para alertar moradores de Middletown que estão no rastro esperado da fumaça da explosão para evacuarem suas casas e irem para um centro de acolhida designado em outro ponto da cidade.

Uma placa de boas-vindas recebe os visitantes da Fábrica de Munições do Exército de Iowa em Middletown — Foto: Zach Boyden-Holmes via REUTERS

O material tóxico foi encontrado em março, em uma fábrica de munições do Exército no sudeste de Iowa. Segundo especialistas militares, a formação de cristais de azida de chumbo dentro dos barris tornou o conteúdo instável e aumentou o risco de uma explosão acidental.

Em documentos apresentados à Justiça, um especialista do Exército afirmou que a redução da quantidade de líquido dentro dos barris aumenta a possibilidade de congelamento da solução.

Isso pode deixar os cristais formados nas paredes e nas tampas dos recipientes ainda mais sensíveis. Até mesmo um pequeno atrito poderia provocar uma reação explosiva em cadeia.

Em comunicado, o Exército afirmou que a operação foi realizada em coordenação com autoridades federais, estaduais e locais e tem o apoio de especialistas.

A Justiça considerou que as medidas de segurança previstas pela Agência de Proteção Ambiental dos EUA eram suficientes para reduzir os riscos. Entre elas estavam a instalação de barreiras, restrições relacionadas às condições meteorológicas e o monitoramento da qualidade do ar.

A decisão também levou em conta que o Exército avaliou diferentes alternativas para eliminar o material.

O Exército afirma que outras alternativas, como o uso de produtos químicos para neutralizar a substância, foram avaliadas. No entanto, a manipulação dos barris poderia aumentar o risco de uma explosão fatal.

Manifestantes em frente ao Centro de Reservas das Forças Armadas em Middletown, Iowa, exigem a suspensão das detonações — Foto: Julie Nickell /The Hawk Eye via AP

Diante dos riscos, moradores de áreas próximas do local onde a explosão deve acontecer começaram a vedar portas e janelas como precaução contra a entrada de partículas de chumbo. A substância é tóxica e pode representar riscos à saúde.

A explosão chegou a ser adiada três vezes após moradores e organizações ambientais manifestarem preocupação com a possível dispersão de partículas de chumbo no ar.

Organizações ambientais contestaram a decisão da Justiça que autorizou a explosão ao afirmar que outras possibilidades não foram analisadas de maneira suficiente.

Outras demonstraram preocupação com a direção que uma eventual nuvem de poeira poderia tomar, dependendo dos ventos.

Autoridades recomendaram que moradores permanecessem dentro de casa durante a explosão e limpem superfícies externas com água depois da operação, para reduzir o contato com possíveis partículas de chumbo.

Os estados vizinhos de Missouri e Illinois também acompanharam a operação, com preocupação sobre possíveis impactos na qualidade do ar e da água.

👉 Especialistas ouvidos pela Associated Press afirmaram que não há uma solução simples para o problema . A azida de chumbo é sensível a calor, congelamento, impactos e atrito. Além disso, o envelhecimento do material aumenta a instabilidade dos explosivos .

articles.title: Cerca de 2 mil migrantes chegam a ilha nas Canárias em um único dia | G1
articles.standfirst: Chegada de migrantes à ilha de El Hierro, que compõe arquipélago das Canárias, na Espanha, bateu recorde nesta semana. Apenas na primeira quinzena de novembro, as Ilhas Canárias receberam mais de 11 mil migrantes.
articles.summary: Chegada de migrantes à ilha de El Hierro, que compõe arquipélago das Canárias, na Espanha, bateu recorde nesta semana. Apenas na primeira quinzena de novembro, as Ilhas Canárias receberam mais de 11 mil migrantes.
articles.body:
Barco de madeira carregando 102 migrantes africanos atracado no porto de La Restinga, na ilha de El Hierro, nas Canárias, em 25 de novembro de 2026. — Foto: Antonio Sempere/AFP

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Cerca de 2.000 migrantes chegaram na terça-feira (24) à ilha espanhola de El Hierro, no arquipélago das Canárias, em meio a um aumento expressivo das chegadas de embarcações precárias, segundo dados do serviço espanhol de Salvamento Marítimo obtidos nesta quarta-feira (25) pela agência de notícias AFP.

A estatística representa um recorde de chegadas em um único dia nas Canárias e superou o número de 1.580 pessoas que chegou às ilhas El Hierro, Gran Canaria e Tenerife em 14 de novembro.

Durante o dia e a noite, equipes de resgate socorreram, no cais de La Restinga, passageiros que chegavam amontoados em diferentes embarcações, segundo um jornalista da AFP presente no local.

Entre as pessoas resgatadas na terça-feira, há cidadãos de pelo menos sete países africanos: Gâmbia, Senegal, Guiné, Guiné-Bissau, Burkina Faso, Mauritânia e Mali; além de um refugiado do Iêmen.

"As Canárias não aguentam mais. Vivemos uma pressão migratória sem precedentes", lamentou no X o presidente regional, Fernando Clavijo, que afirmou ter solicitado "uma reunião urgente" à presidente da Comissão Europeia, Ursula von der Leyen, para obter uma "resposta imediata da UE".

"Essas pessoas chegam à Europa, e não é justo que respondamos sozinhos a um drama dessa magnitude", acrescentou Clavijo.

Entre 1º e 15 de novembro, 11.037 pessoas chegaram ao conjunto do arquipélago das Canárias, segundo o Ministério do Interior espanhol. Desde o início deste ano, as chegadas irregulares somam 24.364, contra 14.690 no mesmo período de 2025.

Diante do aumento do fluxo, as autoridades locais de El Hierro declararam, no início de novembro, uma "emergência social" na pequena ilha, que tem quase 12.000 habitantes e fica no sudoeste das Canárias.

O caso nas Ilhas Canárias remonta à crise em Ceuta e Mellilla , territórios ultramarinos espanhóis no extremo norte da África. No fim de julho, mais de 70 mil migrantes chegaram a nado a Ceuta, vindos do Marrocos. A grande maioria retornou pouco depois.

As Canárias são um arquipélago espanhol na costa noroeste da África composto por oito ilhas:

Imigração é tema central das eleições na Espanha

A imigração tornou-se um dos principais temas da campanha para as eleições gerais antecipadas na Espanha , marcadas para o próximo domingo (29).

A oposição de direita e de extrema direita acusa o presidente do governo, o socialista Pedro Sánchez, de adotar uma postura branda demais em relação à imigração.

Sánchez defende uma imigração "regular" para atender às necessidades demográficas e econômicas da Espanha .

"Esperamos que [a quantidade de chegadas de migrantes] possa ser reduzida nos próximos dias", afirmou Sánchez nesta quarta-feira (25), em entrevista à televisão pública espanhola. Ele garantiu estar "conversando" com as autoridades do Senegal e de Gâmbia para reforçar os controles na origem e, assim, frear o fluxo migratório.

As Canárias, assim como a Itália e a Grécia, são uma das principais portas de entrada na Europa para migrantes que fogem da pobreza, dos conflitos e da perseguição.

A rota do Atlântico, da África Ocidental às Ilhas Canárias, é uma das travessias imigratórias mais mortíferas do mundo, já que os imigrantes buscam chegar ao território espanhol apesar do mar agitado, das fortes correntes e das longas distâncias.

articles.title: Carnatal: Semana de Negócios debate impacto do evento em Natal | G1
articles.standfirst: Encontro chega à segunda edição com painéis sobre empreendedorismo, criatividade, comunicação, vendas e gestão. Na edição de 2025, micareta movimentou R$ 155 milhões na economia da capital.
articles.summary: A Semana de Negócios do Carnatal debate o impacto econômico do evento que movimentou R$ 155 milhões e atrai turistas com gasto médio diário de R$ 1,7 mil em Natal.
articles.body:
Semana de Negócios do Carnatal 2026 — Foto: Sérgio Henrique Santos/Inter TV Cabugi

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O Carnatal vai além dos trios elétricos, blocos e camarotes. Pelo segundo ano consecutivo, a micareta promove uma programação voltada ao empreendedorismo e às oportunidades de negócios com a Semana de Negócios Carnatal. A Inter TV transmitirá ao vivo os três dias do evento .

O evento, ocorrido nesta quarta-feira (25), foi resultado de uma parceria com a Fecomércio-RN e o Senac. O encontro discutiu temas como criatividade, comunicação, vendas e gestão, além de apresentar experiências de empreendedores que movimentam a economia durante o evento.

No total, três painéis sobre evolução, criatividade e gestão foram apresentados, com mediação do CEO da Clap Entrenimento, Antônio Torres. Os painéis foram conduzidos por Felinto Filho, diretor do Carnatal; Luciano Kleiber, diretor de inovação e competitividade da Fecomércio-RN; Ravi Brito, presidente da CDL Jovem Natal ; e Diana Petta, gerente de marketing do Midway Mall.

O evento contou ainda com palestras de Stéffano Antunes, CEO e sócio do Grupo Scopo; e Victor Melo, do The Dew, que falaram de suas experiências ao público da Semana de Negócios.

A iniciativa ocorre em meio à expansão do Carnatal como um evento que também impulsiona atividades econômicas em Natal, envolvendo desde trabalhadores autônomos e microempreendedores até os setores de turismo, hotelaria e shopping centers.

Na edição de 2025, o Carnatal reuniu público superior a 130 mil foliões e movimentou R$ 155 milhões na economia natalense, segundo levantamento da Fecomércio-RN.

Os dados apresentados durante a programação mostram que 40% dos foliões têm entre 25 e 34 anos. O levantamento também aponta crescimento no gasto médio diário individual do público desde 2022.

No Carnatal de 2025, os foliões residentes no Rio Grande do Norte gastaram, em média, R$ 863 por dia. Entre os turistas que se hospedaram em Natal durante o evento, a despesa média diária chegou a quase R$ 1,7 mil.

Os números ajudam a dimensionar o impacto da micareta em diferentes atividades econômicas, como alimentação, transporte, hospedagem e comércio.

A edição deste ano do Carnatal está marcada para os dias 5, 6 e 7 de dezembro, em Natal. A programação musical reúne artistas como Bell Marques, Léo Santana, Claudia Leitte, Ivete Sangalo, Anitta e a Banda Grafith.

Além da programação de shows, o evento movimenta uma cadeia de serviços e negócios que envolve empresas de diferentes portes e profissionais de diversos segmentos.

Sand, porém, afirmou que a decisão cabe ao governo federal e disse que o governo Trump deve se basear nas informações reunidas pelos especialistas que acompanham a situação há semanas.

Segundo um professor de química da Universidade de Indiana, o risco de uma explosão acidental também aumenta quanto mais tempo os barris permanecerem armazenados.

A Prefeitura de São Sebastião, por meio da Secretaria de Obras (Seo), iniciou nesta semana os trabalhos de reconstrução da ciclovia da Praia Deserta, na região central do município. A intervenção contempla uma extensão de 1,2 quilômetro e tem prazo previsto de 30 dias para conclusão, com o objetivo de recuperar a estrutura danificada e proporcionar melhores condições de segurança e mobilidade para os usuários.

A obra integra as ações de manutenção e recuperação dos espaços públicos, com foco na melhoria da infraestrutura urbana e na valorização dos locais destinados à circulação de pedestres e ciclistas.

Durante a execução dos serviços, o Departamento de Trânsito, vinculado à Secretaria de Segurança Urbana (Segur), orienta pedestres, ciclistas e usuários de bicicletas elétricas e equipamentos de mobilidade individual autopropelidos a compartilharem os espaços disponíveis de maneira harmoniosa, respeitando a circulação e a segurança de todos.

Com a reconstrução da ciclovia, a administração municipal busca restabelecer as condições adequadas de circulação em um importante trecho da orla, promovendo mais segurança, acessibilidade e incentivo à mobilidade ativa.

A intervenção faz parte do trabalho de recuperação e conservação da infraestrutura urbana desenvolvido pela Prefeitura, priorizando espaços de uso coletivo e garantindo melhores condições de deslocamento para moradores e visitantes.

articles.title: Stafford woman's last Christmas wish inspires hospice appeal
articles.summary: Katharine House Hospice describes helping Madi Foster celebrate Christmas in May as a privilege.
articles.body:
A 22-year-old hospice patient who celebrated Christmas in May, weeks before her death, has inspired a festive appeal at the site that cared for her.

Madi Foster from Stafford fought adrenocortical carcinoma for three years, raising thousands of pounds for life-lengthening treatment abroad.

She spent her final weeks in Katharine House Hospice, where staff in May helped her decorate her room, cooked a Christmas dinner, and dressed up to join her family and friends in festive games.

As the hospice launched its Care this Christmas appeal to raise money for vital services, Foster's dad Craig said the "fantastic" team there had helped grant his daughter's "last wish".

He explained that her type of cancer had been "very aggressive" and that "survival rates are very very low", but she remained optimistic.

"She had seven operations, she had six different types of chemotherapy, she had radiotherapy as well on three occasions.

"She used to say 'I try the best, I'll try anything, I'll do anything to try and help myself'.

"She was still taking medication two, three days before she passed, with just a glimmer of hope that something might work."

She had initially not wanted to go into the hospice, he said, but immediately felt relaxed around the staff.

"The name hospice has certain connotations and understandably, for a 22-year-old, you don't want to be associated with that," he said.

"But actually within an hour of being [there], Madi just felt at home."

The festive celebration came after Foster had been too unwell to celebrate the previous December.

"We did a full Christmas dinner, turkey and stuffing and pigs in blankets - and everything you can imagine that we'd normally do in December we did in May," her dad said.

"It just happened to coincide with the heatwave that we had and it was about 30-odd degrees outside, even warmer in the room due to all the bodies and the food."

He said the staff were "fantastic" and had even bought cards and presents.

"It was just a lovely day and obviously one that we'll look back on forever, just thinking about and remembering with fondness."

The family said they would now celebrate "Madi's Christmas" every year on 24 May.

Inpatient Unit lead nurse Georgia Simmons said staff had got to know the patient well and felt privileged to have helped create a lasting memory.

"She's just such a positive, inspirational, special person," she said.

"And this story is just something that really means a lot to us all. And it's just a great representation of something that hospices and palliative care can provide.

"It was a difficult day, certainly very difficult day, but there was also a lot of laughter in that room. You could hear the laughter down the corridor, people telling jokes, Christmas crackers, Christmas music, in May and that is just something that is just incredibly special."

The hospice provides free care and support to those with incurable illnesses across Stafford and neighbouring areas.

Its Christmas appeal aims to contribute to the £5m needed annually to run its services.

"We are a charity and we are only able to do the things that we do because of the huge generosity and kindness from the public and from our local community," the nurse added.

"By supporting our Care this Christmas appeal, you could help a nurse manage someone's pain, reassure a worried family or give families valuable time together."

articles.title: A Wisconsin Army veteran went to a Craig Morgan concert expecting a night of music; instead, Michael King and his family learned they would receive a new mortgage-free home, with a groundbreaking planned the next day
articles.summary: A country music concert in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, turned into an unexpected celebration for Army veteran Michael King and his family after they were
articles.body: A country music concert in Menomonee Falls, Wisconsin, turned into an unexpected celebration for Army veteran Michael King and his family after they were selected to receive a custom-built home without a mortgage. The surprise announcement came during a benefit performance by country singer Craig Morgan on November 19, with local builder Belman Homes and nonprofit organisation Operation Finally Home joining forces for the project. WISN 12 News and Spectrum News 1 reported that the family had no idea they had already been chosen when they arrived at the event. King attended the concert with his wife, Marissa, and their two children, believing they were there as guests of the nonprofit. The family had expected to participate in an interview the following day as part of the selection process for a potential home. Instead, they discovered that the decision had already been made in their favour.The announcement was delivered by David Belman, president of Belman Homes, alongside Molly Halliday, senior vice president of Operation Finally Home. The organisations confirmed that the family would receive a new home in Waukesha, with a groundbreaking ceremony scheduled for November 20.For King, the announcement carried particular significance given the challenges he has faced since leaving military service. He enlisted in the US Army at 19 in 2004 and served as an infantryman until 2007. During his military career, he was stationed in Germany before being deployed to Kuwait and Iraq in support of combat operations.His service has left him living with several lasting health conditions, including service-connected post-traumatic stress disorder (PTSD), tinnitus and hearing loss. These challenges have continued to affect his everyday life, with his wife and children providing support as the family navigates the long-term effects of his military experience.The home will be built through a partnership between Belman Homes, a Wisconsin-based residential construction company, and Operation Finally Home, a Texas-based nonprofit dedicated to supporting military families and first responders. Founded in 2005, Operation Finally Home works with builders, developers, suppliers and community partners to provide mortgage-free homes, transitional housing and home modifications to veterans, first responders and surviving spouses. According to Spectrum News 1, the organisation has worked on more than 500 projects across 41 states since its establishment.The initiative aims to address housing challenges faced by individuals and families who have experienced significant sacrifices through military or emergency service. Rather than providing temporary assistance alone, its projects are designed to offer long-term stability through accessible and customised housing. Morgan’s involvement also added another connection to military service at the event. The country singer served in the US Army and Army Reserve for 17 years and reenlisted in the Reserves in 2023, according to Spectrum News 1.The Waukesha project is not the first collaboration between Belman Homes and Operation Finally Home in the area. In 2018, the organisations worked together to provide Army Staff Sergeant Mario Joe Davis and his family with a mortgage-free, accessible ranch-style home in the Town of Waukesha. Davis had medically retired after 11 years of service and was living with Parkinson’s disease. For the King family, however, the latest announcement marks the beginning of a new chapter. What they expected to be an ordinary evening of country music instead became the moment they learned they would have a permanent home without the financial burden of a mortgage.You use AI every day. articles.title: Jeff Bezos’ ex-wife MacKenzie Scott gives another $8 million to Atlanta students as her charitable donations cross $26 billion, yet her fortune remains above $27 billion with Amazon shares continuing to rise
articles.summary: MacKenzie Scott has continued directing large sums towards education and community organisations, even as her personal fortune remains among the largest
articles.body: MacKenzie Scott has continued directing large sums towards education and community organisations, even as her personal fortune remains among the largest in the world. As reported, her latest contribution is an $8 million donation to Achieve Atlanta, a nonprofit supporting students from Atlanta's public schools with the cost of higher education. It is the second time Scott has made a gift of the same size to the organisation, taking her contributions to $16 million. The donation comes as the philanthropist's cumulative charitable giving has crossed $26 billion. Yet, despite the scale of those contributions, her wealth is still estimated to exceed $27 billion, helped in part by the performance of Amazon shares.MacKenzie Scott's $8 million gift helps Atlanta students pursue collegeAchieve Atlanta confirmed the latest contribution last week, four years after Scott first donated $8 million to the organisation. Its work centres on helping graduates of Atlanta Public Schools move into higher education, with financial assistance and guidance extending beyond the initial college application.The scholarship programme provides different levels of support depending on the type of institution students attend. Those pursuing a four-year bachelor's degree can receive need-based assistance of up to $20,000 across four years. Students enrolled in two-year colleges or technical programmes are eligible for annual awards of $1,500, available for as many as four semesters.Students also receive help with identifying suitable colleges, completing applications and preparing for employment after graduation. Achieve Atlanta Scholars confirmed its establishment in 2015, and has distributed more than $75 million in scholarships.What six-year graduation figures reveal about the scholarship programmeThe organisation's work has also been examined through an independent assessment involving researchers associated with Georgia State University's Georgia Policy Labs. The evaluation compared Achieve Atlanta scholarship recipients with other graduates of Atlanta Public Schools who had similar academic and demographic backgrounds but entered college without the programme's financial support.The findings showed a difference in how students progressed after enrolling. Fortune reported, around 91% of scholarship recipients returned for their second semester, against 77% of students in the comparison group. Six years after completing high school, 42% of the students who had received Achieve Atlanta support had graduated from college. The corresponding figure among comparable students without the programme's assistance was 36%.Achieve Atlanta referred to Scott's second contribution as recognition of its approach to supporting students beyond high school. The organisation said the continued funding would help sustain its postsecondary education work.A separate $4.5 million contribution supports women returning to educationScott's latest charitable activity in Georgia has not been limited to young people entering college. Another education-focused organisation, the Jeannette Rankin Foundation, confirmed $4.5 million from the philanthropist. Based in Athens, Georgia, the foundation works with women aged 35 and older who want to pursue education but face financial barriers. The contribution is its largest single donation to date, according to The Atlanta Journal-Constitution.Foundation chief executive Karen Sterk told the newspaper that the funding could potentially benefit more than one million women. The organisation's work focuses on making educational opportunities accessible to women who may have had to put their studies aside because of financial circumstances or other responsibilities.Why Scott's wealth has remained above $27 billionScott's charitable giving has reached a scale that would substantially reduce most personal fortunes. Her own financial position, however, has been shaped by the continued appreciation of the Amazon shares she received following her divorce from Jeff Bezos. The couple finalised their divorce in July 2019 after 25 years of marriage. Under the settlement, Scott received approximately 4% of Amazon, with the stake valued at around $37 billion at the time, as reported by Fortune.Since then, she has distributed more than $26 billion through over 2,700 donations to nonprofit organisations, according to Yield Giving, the philanthropic organisation she established. Forbes nevertheless estimates her current net worth at more than $27 billion.Her ownership of Amazon has reduced considerably. A regulatory filing showed that her holdings in the company fell by 42% during the year ending September 2025. The value of the shares she continues to hold has also changed the picture. Amazon's stock gained more than 42% over the five-year period ending in July 2026, according to figures previously reported by Fortune. The increase has helped offset the financial impact of her substantial charitable contributions.Amazon's position in the corporate world has also strengthened. The company secured the top position in the 2026 Fortune 500 ranking, becoming the largest US company by revenue and ending Walmart's 13-year run at the top of the list.MacKenzie Scott backs HBCUs and charities with billions in donationsScott's education-related contributions have followed a pattern of supporting institutions and communities that often receive less attention from major donors. Her giving has included historically Black colleges and universities (HBCUs), community colleges and tribal colleges, rather than being concentrated among the country's best-known private universities.Her donations to HBCUs alone have exceeded $1 billion, Fortune has reported. Other major contributions have reached organisations working in areas such as housing, children's welfare and reproductive healthcare. Among her largest reported gifts are $436 million to Habitat for Humanity, $281 million to Boys & Girls Clubs of America and $275 million to Planned Parenthood.Scott also joined the Giving Pledge in 2019, committing to give away most of her wealth during her lifetime or through her will. The initiative was established by philanthropists Warren Buffett and Bill and Melinda Gates to encourage wealthy individuals to dedicate the majority of their fortunes to charitable causes.MacKenzie Scott looks beyond donations to support social impact businessesHer philanthropic plans extend beyond transferring money directly to nonprofit organisations. In a 2024 Yield Giving essay, Scott discussed how she wanted her investment portfolio to support some of the same causes that guide her charitable contributions. She explained that she had asked her investment team to identify funds and businesses addressing social challenges, including affordable housing and digital healthcare services for women. The intention was to direct capital towards enterprises working in areas where she also wanted to make a difference through philanthropy.Scott also described a preference for investments in businesses led by people who understand the communities they serve. This includes founders from backgrounds that can make it harder to secure conventional funding, particularly women and people of colour.In her 2019 Giving Pledge letter, Scott had already outlined her intention to continue distributing her wealth rather than wait for a later stage of life. She wrote that the process would require time, effort and care, but that she would continue until her fortune had been given away.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Britain's RAF moves warplanes into hangars at night amid drone fears, considers anti-drone nets
articles.summary: The Royal Air Force is implementing nighttime relocations of military aircraft and considering anti-drone nets to safeguard against potential drone attacks, amid rising security fears related to Iranian threats against key UK bases.
articles.body: The Royal Air Force (RAF) is moving military aircraft into hangars and hardened shelters under cover of darkness as part of efforts to protect them from potential drone attacks, Sky News reported.The air force is also considering installing anti-drone nets around aircraft that cannot be moved into protected facilities and remain exposed near runways or at airbases with limited security infrastructure.The aircraft movements come as security concerns grow around RAF bases and other military facilities in Britain. Iran is suspected of plotting an attack against RAF Fairford in Gloucestershire, an installation also used by the US Air Force. The reported threat led the Pentagon to move bomber aircraft away from the base. US warplanes have also been relocated from another British airbase following reports of a separate Iranian threat, as per the outlet.The RAF's preparations also include practising the rapid movement of aircraft between locations to reduce the risk of having its fleet concentrated at a small number of airfields.Air Chief Marshal Sir Harv Smyth said the service was preparing for a situation in which military aircraft could no longer rely on the safety of their home bases."There is no sanctuary at home, you are fighting from the UK but you need to get on the move," he said at an event hosted by the Freeman Air and Space Institute on Tuesday evening.Smyth pointed to the RAF's recent experience of moving aircraft while a new runway was being constructed at RAF Brize Norton, its main air transport base. During the work, aircraft were dispersed between locations including Prestwick in Scotland and Boscombe Down in Wiltshire.He said the exercise demonstrated the RAF's ability to shift aircraft across the country while maintaining operations."As a service, we have proved that if we need to, we can take what people would have called 'eggs in one basket' and spread it across the length of the United Kingdom and keep operating," Smyth said."That was a big test for us and frankly the team nailed it."The air chief added that the RAF needed to conduct more such exercises to ensure its aircraft and personnel were prepared for potential conflict.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'Voluntary return plan separate from Bangladesh extradition request': India on Sheikh Hasina
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Ahead of Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh on December 16, India on Wednesday described the matter as \"separate\" from Dhaka's
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Ahead of Sheikh Hasina's planned return to Bangladesh on December 16, India on Wednesday described the matter as "separate" from Dhaka's request to extradite the former prime minister."The case of a citizen willing to return voluntarily to her country on a travel document is a matter separate from an extradition request," ministry of external affairs (MEA) spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal told reporters at a press conference in New Delhi.However, he did not elaborate.Jaiswal reiterated that Bangladesh's extradition request for Sheikh Hasina was being examined in accordance with established procedures."The extradition request, as I've said earlier, is being examined in line with our established processes," he added.The MEA's statement came a day after Sheikh Hasina's spokesperson announced that she would return to Bangladesh on December 16, when the country celebrates its victory over Pakistan in the 1971 Liberation War.Sheikh Hasina had also requested the Bangladesh government, now led by Tarique Rahman, son of her long-time political rival Khaleda Zia, to issue the necessary travel documents. However, the request was turned down.The former prime minister has been living in India since fleeing Bangladesh on August 5, 2024, following a student-led uprising that brought down her 15-year government. In November 2025, she was sentenced to death in absentia for crimes against humanity over the crackdown on protesters in 2024.She has rejected the charges and expressed her intention to return to Bangladesh and surrender before a court.In July, ahead of the second anniversary of her resignation, Sheikh Hasina had, for the first time, announced a specific timeline for her return to Bangladesh, saying she planned to return in December.Bangladesh has been seeking her extradition from India, while New Delhi has maintained that Dhaka's request is being examined through established legal processes. The issue has become a source of tension between the two countries, with Dhaka insisting that Hasina be handed over under the bilateral extradition treaty.(With PTI inputs)Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday clarified its decision to issue a show-cause notice to Cockroach Janata Party leader Saurav Das,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The ministry of external affairs on Wednesday clarified its decision to issue a show-cause notice to Cockroach Janata Party leader Saurav Das, saying that a discrepancy amounting to suppression of facts was reported in his passport application.During the bi-weekly press briefing, MEA spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that the ministry allows applicants to present their side if a discrepancy is noted or reported by the authorities."The passport application process requires the applicant to provide accurate information. If, at any stage, a discrepancy is noted or reported by the authorities, amounting to a suppression of facts, we issue a show-cause notice to the applicant, allowing them to present their side of the matter," Jaiswal said.Also read| 'Voluntary return plan separate from Bangladesh extradition request': India on Sheikh Hasina"Based on reports received from the relevant law enforcement authorities, the Regional Passport Office (RPO) in Chennai issued a show-cause notice to Saurav Das on November 23, 2026, requesting a clarification within seven days regarding his place of birth. He was also advised not to use the passport until he had submitted his response," he added.Jaiswal said that passport applicants must provide accurate information and that any discrepancies flagged by authorities are addressed through a show-cause notice seeking an explanation."When an individual applies for a passport and fills out the application form, it is implicit that they must provide correct information. If we identify any shortcomings or discrepancies, brought to our attention by the authorities, the established procedure is to issue a show-cause notice to the applicant (or the passport holder)," Jaiswal said."This notice asks the individual to explain the discrepancies or inconsistencies that have emerged in relation to the information they originally provided," he added.Also read| Iranian delegation meets MEA officials to discuss multilateral tiesSubsequently, the Regional Passport Office (RPO), Chennai, served a notice to the CJP activist asking him to explain alleged discrepancies in his documents relating to his place of birth. His passport was rendered ineligible for foreign travel until he responded to the notice and the matter was resolved.According to sources, the department flagged mismatches in his birth particulars across different documents, including Aadhaar, passport and birth certificate, based on inputs received over the last couple of months. articles.title: 5 Maharashtra districts face fast-building flash droughts; Beed, Solapur among hotspots
articles.summary: MUMBAI: With Maharashtra's 2026 monsoon ending 13% below normal, a new scientific study has identified five districts — Ahilyanagar, Beed, Dharashiv,
articles.body: MUMBAI: With Maharashtra's 2026 monsoon ending 13% below normal, a new scientific study has identified five districts — Ahilyanagar, Beed, Dharashiv, Sangli and Solapur — as the state's most vulnerable flash-drought hotspots, where agricultural land can rapidly shift from normal moisture conditions to severe dryness within a few weeks.The findings raise concerns over the preparedness of farmers and district administrations ahead of the next monsoon, particularly in the semi-arid interior, where rainfall-dependent agriculture is vulnerable to sudden spells of intense drying. Unlike conventional droughts, which develop over months or seasons, flash droughts intensify rapidly, leaving little time for farmers to respond or authorities to arrange contingency measures.The 44-year analysis, conducted by Vikas Poonia and Deepika Yadav of the Maulana Azad National Institute of Technology (MANIT), Bhopal, examined rainfall, temperature, soil moisture and evaporation patterns across all 36 Maharashtra districts between 1981 and 2024. Published in the peer-reviewed journal Physics and Chemistry of the Earth in October 2026, it found that the five identified districts experienced the most severe and fastest-building episodes.The study found that soil dryness in these five districts worsened by six to nine percentile points every eight days, exceeding nine points in some locations. Across most other parts of Maharashtra, the deterioration was below six percentile points over the same period."The semi-arid interior districts of Ahilyanagar, Beed, Dharashiv, Sangli and Solapur are where flash droughts happen most severely and most quickly. A field can move from normal moisture to severe dryness in a matter of weeks, without the warning associated with a conventional drought," said Poonia, assistant professor in MANIT's department of civil engineering and corresponding author of the study.Pre-monsoon weeks emerge as critical windowThe research found that flash droughts were uncommon during the monsoon, when regular rainfall generally maintained soil moisture. Most districts recorded fewer than two such events during the monsoon months over the 44-year period.The situation was markedly different during the dry months. Districts recorded an average of around 20 flash-drought events over the study period, with most reporting between five and 25. Solapur, Dharashiv, Ratnagiri and Sindhudurg recorded more than 25 events, typically lasting 20 to 25 days.The most vulnerable period was the transition from the dry season to the monsoon. During these pre-monsoon weeks, when temperatures peak but rainfall has yet to arrive, several parts of Maharashtra experienced the most frequent and longest-lasting flash droughts, with some episodes continuing for 30 to 40 days.This seasonal vulnerability is particularly relevant after the deficient 2026 monsoon, given the dependence of a large part of the state's agriculture on rainfall. The study notes that about 83% of Maharashtra's land is semi-arid and nearly 88% of its annual rainfall occurs during the four monsoon months.Rain deficit triggers drought, heat accelerates itThe researchers found that a rainfall shortfall was generally the starting point, while high temperatures and dry atmospheric conditions determined how rapidly the drought intensified.Heat alone rarely triggered flash droughts. However, when high temperatures coincided with an existing dry spell, soil moisture declined much faster. Around Solapur, deficient rainfall, high temperatures and already-dry soil acted together. In eastern districts such as Wardha, Yavatmal and Nagpur, high temperatures played a significant role in accelerating the drying process.As flash droughts developed, soil moisture declined by around 17 percentile points, while the atmosphere became hotter and drier. This increased the vapour pressure deficit — a measure of how strongly the atmosphere draws moisture from soil and vegetation — further accelerating moisture loss."Rain failure is usually what starts a flash drought, but it is heat and dry air on top of that dry spell that decide how bad it gets. Monitoring systems need to watch temperature and soil moisture as closely as rainfall, especially in the weeks before the monsoon," said co-author Deepika Yadav.Interestingly, wetter eastern districts such as Gadchiroli, Chandrapur and Bhandara also experienced flash droughts, but these were generally less severe and slower to intensify. Coastal districts such as Ratnagiri, Palghar, Thane and Sindhudurg also recorded milder episodes, attributed to relatively higher rainfall and humid conditions.Drought frequency rising in 2 districtsWhile most districts did not show a statistically significant long-term change, the study identified emerging hotspots. Flash-drought frequency increased significantly in Dharashiv and Washim, while the speed of intensification increased significantly in Solapur and Sindhudurg. Several other districts showed weaker indications of faster intensification.The authors said the findings point to a geographically concentrated risk rather than a uniform deterioration across Maharashtra.IIT-B portal offers four-week forecastsA potential tool for strengthening preparedness is IIT Bombay's KrishiDrought.in portal, developed by Prof Karthikeyan Lanka's Ecohydrology group. The public platform provides weekly agricultural drought forecasts up to four weeks ahead at the district level, combining satellite-based soil-moisture data, weather records and deep-learning models.By tracking soil moisture alongside rainfall, temperature and atmospheric dryness, the platform monitors several of the indicators associated with flash drought development in the MANIT study. It could help farmers and district authorities in vulnerable areas such as Beed, Solapur and Dharashiv identify developing dry spells earlier.The researchers recommend integrating such monitoring into district-level drought preparedness, water management and climate-resilient farming plans. They have also urged authorities to issue early warnings based on multiple indicators rather than relying exclusively on rainfall data.Poonia cautioned that the research did not examine El Niño's influence on flash droughts. However, with El Niño conditions expected to continue into early 2027, he urged farmers and district administrations in the identified hotspots to prepare for a potentially hotter and drier pre-monsoon period.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Mumbai | Silver Rate in Mumbai | Bank Holidays in Mumbai | Public Holidays in Mumbai | Mumbai AQI | Weather in Mumbai | Petrol Price in Mumbai | Diesel Price in Mumbai | CNG Price in Mumbai | LPG Price in MumbaiStay updated with the latest Mumbai news. articles.title: US Thanksgiving airfares average $469, up 57% from last year, as repeated airline system failures push families toward road trips and forecasts show nearly 29 million people will fly over the holiday
articles.summary: Families travelling across the United States for Thanksgiving face higher ticket prices and new worries about flight delays after airline tech failures
articles.body: Families travelling across the United States for Thanksgiving face higher ticket prices and new worries about flight delays after airline tech failures hit services in November. Domestic flights average $469, which is up 57% from last year, pushing some travellers to drive instead of risking expensive trips and more delays. Airlines for America forecasts nearly 29 million flyers between November 20 and 30, down from the 31 million forecast for the same days last year as steep prices and recent flight problems shape holiday plans.A nationwide ground stop ordered by the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) on November 13 added to fears about flying after a communications breakdown at air traffic control centres hit more than 18,000 flights and about one million travellers, according to Reuters. A few days later, more tech glitches at United Airlines and Delta Air Lines delayed over 2,000 flights nationwide right before one of the busiest travel weeks of the year, leaving some flyers unsure they would get where they were going on time.Higher fares change holiday plansFor Dinese Jackson, flying from Raleigh, North Carolina, to Dallas, Texas, with her two children cost too much. The 51-year-old credit analyst faced a bill of about $1,500, more than double what she had paid for similar trips in past years. She kept checking fares hoping they would drop, then the FAA's nationwide ground stop on November 13 led her to drive instead, even though the trip takes 17 hours."When that happened on Friday, I was like, 'Yep, I'm keeping my car reservation. I'm going to go ahead and drive for sure," Jackson told Reuters. "For those that are flying, I just think it's going to ​be chaos."Ticket prices have climbed for months, with travel search engine Kayak finding that domestic Thanksgiving airfares averaged about $469 two weeks before the 2026 holiday, up 57% from the same time last year. Booking app Hopper said higher jet fuel costs over several months, tied to the conflict in Iran, helped push Thanksgiving and Christmas fares to a 10-year high. Higher prices have also shaped flyer numbers, as the Transportation Security Administration (TSA) has not screened more than three million people in a single day in 2026 after hitting that mark eight times in 2025, last doing so on November 30, and expects to screen about 3% fewer travellers this Thanksgiving than last year.Recent system failures add to concernsThe November 13 trouble started when a router outage caused a communications failure at air traffic control centres, leading to a nationwide ground stop lasting nearly five hours that affected over 18,000 flights and about one million travellers. More problems followed when United Airlines had a wide tech outage days later and Delta Air Lines' automated weight-and-balance system failed on Sunday, delaying more than 2,000 flights across the country. These failures worry travellers who are already paying more to fly, while the FAA also warned that stormy weather could disrupt flights during the week, creating another risk during the holiday rush.Jennifer Shaw, 57, felt uneasy after her son gave up his non-refundable flight home from college in Michigan and planned a 10-hour drive to Monmouth County, New Jersey, with friends. "Even though I might be worried that he's driving 10 hours ​with a group of boys, at least I ​don't have to worry about the airlines," Shaw told Reuters.FAA pauses further equipment upgradesThe FAA still has not given a full explanation for the router failure. FAA Administrator Bryan Bedford said last week that the agency was "very close" to finding the root cause, though the agency would not say on Monday when an update would come. On November 17, the FAA announced an immediate pause on putting in more routers. That pause worries some people planning to fly for the holiday, including 63-year-old retiree Liz Dougherty, who is set to fly from North Carolina to Spain for a Thanksgiving cruise and said recent flight troubles were on her mind."I'm hoping the government is not going to do any more ​upgrades during this time that ⁠we're going to be away," Dougherty told Reuters, adding that the November 13 flight halt was "definitely in the back of my mind." The pause on new equipment rollouts comes as airports get ready for heavy holiday traffic, and millions of Americans will still travel over Thanksgiving even with fewer flyers than last year.Buses and trains see more bookingsAs fewer people choose to fly, demand has grown for other ways to travel. According to the American Automobile Association (AAA), about 81.5 million Americans will travel at least 50 miles over a six-day Thanksgiving period, just under the 81.6 million recorded last year, with more people expected to take cruises, buses and trains this year. Bus and travel search site Wanderu said the November 13 ground stop gave it its busiest booking day of the year so far, with Friday bookings up about 16% from the same day last year. Bus company Flix North America also saw higher demand, with Thanksgiving bookings rising 17% from 2025, while Amtrak expects another record year after handling 1.2 million customer trips during last year's Thanksgiving holiday and saying demand should reach a new high in 2026.Airlines prepare for millions of passengersEven with higher fares and recent disruptions, big airlines are getting ready to carry millions of travellers over the holiday. United Airlines expects to fly more than 6.6 million customers over 12 days, roughly matching last year's total, while American Airlines expects about eight million travellers over that same stretch and plans to run 4% more flights than in 2025. Across the US airline industry, carriers are running an average of 2% more flights this Thanksgiving than last year, with seat capacity up 1%, according to flight analytics firm Cirium. These numbers show airlines are keeping or growing their schedules even as some travellers pick other transport, gearing up for big crowds while recent tech failures and high fares shift how some families plan their trips. For flyers, the FAA's warning about possible storms adds another worry during Thanksgiving week, whereas high ticket costs and delay risks have already made up the minds of others like Jackson, who is keeping her car booking for the 17-hour drive to Texas.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Michigan widow once won more than $78 million after a truck crash killed her husband and son; an appeals court has now thrown out $24 million for their pre-impact fear and ordered a retrial on $19 million
articles.summary: A Michigan appeals court has overturned $24 million awarded to a widow for the fear her husband and son may have felt moments before a fatal lorry crash,
articles.body: A Michigan appeals court has overturned $24 million awarded to a widow for the fear her husband and son may have felt moments before a fatal lorry crash, ruling that state wrongful-death law does not allow compensation for pre-impact fright and shock. The court has also ordered a new trial over $19 million awarded for the pair’s conscious pain and suffering, leaving other parts of a judgment worth more than $78 million intact. The ruling was issued on 20 November 2026 by the Michigan Court of Appeals in a case brought by Natalie Attianese, whose husband, Jude, and 20-year-old son, Zachary, died in the crash on Interstate 75 in June 2018. The original jury award, including interest, was $78,517,580.94.How the fatal crash happenedThe collision happened on the night of 15 June 2018, as the family travelled from New Jersey to Michigan for a funeral in Sterling Heights. Jude Attianese, 56, was driving north on I-75 with Zachary in the passenger seat. They were moving at about three miles per hour in slow traffic caused by roadworks. Jose Angel Nogueras, who was driving an 18-wheel lorry for Canadian trucking company Challenger Motor Freight, approached from behind. He failed to stop and struck their car at more than 50 miles per hour. The impact pushed their vehicle forward into the car in front, causing a second collision.The court's opinion said Nogueras had Parkinson's disease and was taking medication that made him drowsy at the time. There was no evidence that he applied the brakes before hitting the Attianeses' vehicle. Both men suffered fatal injuries, including internal decapitation and bleeding around the brain. An eyewitness who reached the car after the crash said neither man was moving or appeared to be breathing. Police officers also found them unresponsive. Natalie filed a lawsuit against Nogueras and Challenger in November 2019. The defendants admitted that Nogueras had been negligent and that Challenger was responsible for the deaths. They later admitted liability for all claims, leaving the trial to focus on the amount of compensation.Jury awarded more than $78 millionThe trial took place in April 2023 and focused on damages. The jury heard evidence about whether Jude and Zachary had been aware of the approaching lorry, whether they suffered before dying and how their deaths affected Natalie. The court heard testimony from witnesses who said the lorry could be seen and heard approaching. One driver, Lawrence Chockley, said he saw it coming in his rear-view mirror and feared it would not stop before reaching the traffic queue.The jury awarded $12 million each for Jude and Zachary's fear and shock before the collision, making a combined $24 million. It also awarded $8 million for Jude's conscious pain and suffering and $11 million for Zachary's. Natalie received a further $9 million for the loss of society and companionship for each man from the date of the crash until the trial. The jury also awarded future damages for the loss of their company, including payments calculated over periods extending to 2039 for Jude and 2076 for Zachary. After adjustments for future payments and interest, the trial court entered a judgment of $78,517,580.94. That included about $71.2 million in past non-economic damages and $7.28 million in future non-economic damages. The defendants challenged the verdict, arguing that some of the damages were not permitted under Michigan law and that the trial had included evidence and testimony that unfairly affected the jury's decision.Why the appeals court removed $24 millionThe appeals court said the $24 million award for pre-impact fright and shock could not stand under Michigan's wrongful-death law. Its decision relied on a Michigan Supreme Court ruling in Daher v Prime Healthcare Services-Garden City, issued in July 2024, after the original trial court had rejected the defendants' post-trial challenge. The law allows certain types of compensation in wrongful-death cases, including reasonable payment for pain and suffering experienced while the person was conscious between the time of injury and death. The appeals court said the law does not allow a separate award for fear experienced before the injury itself. Natalie had argued that the fear Jude and Zachary experienced when they realised the lorry was about to hit them should count as part of their injury. The appeals court rejected that argument, saying there was no evidence of physical consequences before the collision. It therefore ruled that the jury had no legal basis to award separate damages for pre-impact fright and shock. The full $24 million award was set aside.$19 million pain and suffering award faces retrialThe court also ordered a new trial over the $19 million awarded for conscious pain and suffering. It did not rule that the claim itself was invalid. Instead, it found that the trial judge had made a mistake by allowing a replacement medical expert to testify without giving the defence enough notice or a fair chance to examine his opinions. Natalie's original medical expert, Dr Lawrence Shields, was unable to testify on the revised trial schedule. Dr Kenneth Mankowski was brought in to replace him. The appeals court said the defence had not received the required details of Mankowski's opinions and was not allowed to question him before he gave evidence.Mankowski told the jury that Jude may have remained conscious for about 65 to 70 seconds after the crash, while Zachary may have been conscious for around three minutes. He said they could have realised they were unable to breathe. The jury's awards of $8 million and $11 million were based on this testimony. The defence's medical expert, Dr Ljubisa Dragovic, disagreed. He said the injuries caused by the collision led to immediate unconsciousness and death. The appeals court said the question of whether the two men experienced conscious pain and suffering could properly be decided by a jury, but the replacement expert's testimony had been admitted unfairly. It sent the issue back for a new trial, giving the defence an opportunity to examine the evidence properly.Other parts of the judgment remain in placeThe appeals court rejected the defendants' request for a new trial on all issues. It found that some evidence about liability should not have been presented, but said this did not justify reopening the entire case. It also upheld the awards for loss of society and companionship. The defendants had argued that the verdict was excessive, but the court noted that their own lawyer had suggested a similar annual figure for future damages during the original trial. The final ruling therefore leaves the compensation for the family's loss in place while removing the $24 million pre-impact award and sending the $19 million pain and suffering claim back to a jury. The case, Estate of Zachary Attianese v Jose Angel Nogueras, was decided by the Michigan Court of Appeals on 20 November 2026.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: Felix “xQc” Lengyel has questioned why GTA 6 voice actor Lexie Shoaibi appeared on HasanAbi’s livestream despite what he believes are her differences with the political commentator. Shoaibi, who voices Mandy in the upcoming game, joined Hasan’s broadcast on November 22, 2026, and openly admitted that she was already following him. Two days later, xQc discussed her appearance on his livestream and made several comments about her political views. HasanAbi also responded to the criticism on X, sharing three question marks without adding any explanation.xQc Questions Lexie Shoaibi’s Support for HasanAbi After Her GTA 6 Livestream AppearanceThe discussion started after Shoaibi joined HasanAbi’s livestream on November 22. During their conversation, Hasan told her that a mutual friend had informed him she was a fan of his content. He also mentioned that he had checked her social media profile and found her views familiar.Shoaibi agreed with his comment and replied, “Super woke, was already following you. Yeah. Of course!”Her appearance was also a chance for viewers to meet the person behind Mandy, a character in Rockstar Games’ Grand Theft Auto 6. However, it was her support for Hasan that later became the subject of xQc’s comments.During his November 24 livestream, the French-Canadian streamer questioned the connection. He claimed that Hasan was Shoaibi’s “arch nemesis,” referring to what he said she had posted on TikTok. He also questioned why she would appear on Hasan’s broadcast if she had such strong differences with him.xQc said:“Of course, she's a Hasan Tier three sub (Twitch subscriber). Of course, a ******* ****** is a Hasan sub. Chat, this was the golden opportunity to jump at a white CIS male. I mean, this is her arch nemesis, according to her TikTok - she hates him! So why did she jump on him, buddy? Explain it. Explain it then. Oh, because he woke up and he wasn't white today. My bad. My bad. My bad. I get it. Today, he chose a different suit. I get it. All good.”The streamer then moved on to the subject of race and ethnicity. He argued that people sometimes change how they describe these identities depending on the situation.He added:“No, people will tailor their definition of what is ethnicity, what is race, and what is being color on a day-to-day basis. They will switch it up. Oh, yeah! 'I'm white, but of color, Middle Eastern, Canadian, Turkish.' Yo, I mean, yo, buddy, you're shifting; we get it, man.”HasanAbi Reacts to xQc’s Comments About Lexie Shoaibi and Her GTA 6 RoleHasanAbi also addressed the situation on November 24. He quote-tweeted a post from the account @xQc_dailyy, which featured a clip of xQc talking about Shoaibi. Instead of writing a longer response or arguing against his comments, Hasan posted three question marks.The short response did not explain what he thought about xQc's remarks. However, it showed that Hasan had seen the clip and was aware of the criticism directed at his guest.There is also an important difference between what happened during the original livestream and what xQc claimed later. Shoaibi openly said she followed Hasan and was familiar with his content. However, the claim that Hasan was her arch nemesis came from xQc's interpretation of her TikTok posts. It was not something she said during the November 22 conversation.The two livestreams therefore presented different sides of the discussion. Shoaibi's appearance was a friendly interaction with a streamer whose content she already followed, while xQc questioned the apparent difference between that support and her views on social media.As of November 25, the reported exchange had drawn reactions from both streamers, but no direct response from Shoaibi to xQc's criticism was included in the available reports.You use AI every day. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: While the Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed Allahabad high court’s order directing a probe into the assets of the leader of opposition Rahul
articles.body: NEW DELHI: While the Supreme Court on Wednesday quashed Allahabad high court’s order directing a probe into the assets of the leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi, it did not consider Rahul Gandhi’s plea for transfer of the PIL to any other HC or the SC.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal said HC adopted a process “completely unknown to law” while passing the impugned order as it did not even seek Gandhi’s response and permitted a witch-hunt without questioning the petitioner’s locus standi.The bench of CJI Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana said that HC, during the fresh hearing on Vignesh’s PIL, would hear Gandhi’s submissions against the petition, including the maintainability of such a petition before a constitutional court and the locus standi of the petitioner to raise such issues through a writ petition.On August 17, SC had barred CBI, ED or any other authority from filing any report before HC pursuant to its July 20 order and directed HC to defer the proceedings till further orders. For CBI, additional solicitor general S V Raju had told the court that CBI is only verifying the complaint and has not commenced a probe yet. “CBI has not registered even a preliminary enquiry. The complaint may be wrong or right on facts. If they are right, then it is a gross case of disproportionate assets,” he had said.CJI Kant had said, “In our understanding of the law, police or any probe agency, if they have prima facie material they can register a case, investigate it and can proceed against anyone. No permission is required from the accused. But what appears to us, subject to assistance from both sides, is that if the court wants to issue a direction, it is expected to follow principles of natural justice.”Gandhi, in his special leave petition, had said, “Since 2024, Shishir, who, it appears from public reporting, is a member of BJP — a party whose politics and ideology the Petitioner (Gandhi) and his party (Congress) vehemently contest — has instituted multiple proceedings before different forums, including successive PILs concerning the Petitioner’s alleged foreign citizenship and criminal proceedings seeking registration of an FIR...”Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: A 65-acre New Jersey woodland has opened as a protected nature preserve after conservation groups bought it to prevent development, adding habitat for bobcats and eagles to a growing wildlife corridor
articles.summary: A stretch of forested land in northwestern New Jersey has received permanent protection, creating a new public nature preserve and strengthening a wider
articles.body: A stretch of forested land in northwestern New Jersey has received permanent protection, creating a new public nature preserve and strengthening a wider effort to safeguard wildlife habitats across the region. The 65-acre property, named Lone Wolf Preserve, is located in Frankford Township, Sussex County, near Branchville. According to the New Jersey Conservation Foundation, The Nature Conservancy and local reporting by Daily Voice, the acquisition was made possible through a partnership of conservation organisations, government funding programmes and local donations. The Greater Culver Lake Watershed Conservation Foundation announced the opening on November 19, confirming that the property would remain protected from development while allowing visitors to enjoy hiking, birdwatching and other low-impact outdoor activities. The woodland borders Stokes State Forest and contains a stream originating from Lake Owassa that eventually flows into Culver Lake. Protecting the surrounding forest and wetlands is expected to help maintain water quality while preserving habitat for native wildlife. The New Jersey Department of Environmental Protection has identified the property as a core area for wildlife connectivity through its Connecting Habitat Across New Jersey (CHANJ) initiative.The preserve provides important habitat for species including bald eagles, red-shouldered hawks and bobcats, although the presence of these animals on the property is not guaranteed. Its location alongside existing protected landscapes makes the acquisition particularly valuable for wildlife that depends on connected forest habitats. The purchase was coordinated with assistance from Conservation Advising Services, which worked with the landowner and conservation partners to secure the necessary funding. Financial support came from New Jersey’s Green Acres programme, The Nature Conservancy and the New Jersey Conservation Foundation through the Open Space Institute’s Delaware River Watershed Protection Fund, alongside contributions from local residents.The Greater Culver Lake Watershed Conservation Foundation will own the property and manage it in partnership with the Lake Owassa-Paulins Kill Headwaters Conservation Foundation. Lone Wolf Preserve also builds on an earlier conservation effort in the township. Over the past three years, the same partnership has helped permanently protect another 268 acres through the creation of Culver Brook Preserve and Culver Brook Preserve East. The two properties include a former golf course covering 95 acres and an adjoining 173-acre forested parcel. Together, the three conservation projects have secured 333 acres of additional protected land in the area.The latest acquisition also contributes to a much larger regional initiative known as Bobcat Alley, led by The Nature Conservancy. Covering approximately 96,000 acres across northwestern New Jersey, the landscape connects important natural areas along the Appalachian Mountain range, including Stokes State Forest, the Kittatinny Ridge and sections of the Highlands. The initiative aims to protect an additional 10,000 acres within Bobcat Alley by 2030, bringing the proportion of conserved land in the region to approximately 40%. The Nature Conservancy reports that more than 2,600 acres towards this target have already been protected through partnerships with local organisations and landowners. The corridor is particularly important for New Jersey’s bobcat population.The species is listed as threatened in the state, and habitat fragmentation caused by roads, construction and expanding development has made it increasingly difficult for wildlife to move safely between natural areas. According to The Nature Conservancy, connected habitats also benefit numerous other species, including birds, amphibians and mammals that depend on the Appalachian landscape.Beyond wildlife protection, the preservation of forested land around Lake Owassa and Culver Lake carries significant environmental benefits for nearby communities. Forests, wetlands and feeder streams help filter water, reduce runoff and maintain the health of freshwater ecosystems that support local residents and wildlife. For Frankford Township, the opening of Lone Wolf Preserve represents another step in protecting its natural landscape against development pressure. By adding another permanently conserved property to an expanding network of forests and wetlands, conservation groups hope to create more connected habitats where wildlife can move, feed and thrive.You use AI every day. articles.title: Cwmbran mum rebuilds life after bioethanol heater fire explosion
articles.summary: Saffron Carthew spent five weeks in a coma after a bioethanol table top fire exploded in her face.
articles.body:
A mother is trying to rebuild her life after a summer evening with family and friends "turned into a nightmare" when her table top heater exploded.

Saffron Carthew had fourth-degree burns and severe injuries from smoke inhalation before being placed in an induced coma for five weeks after the July explosion caused her skin and hair to "fall off".

She had bought the fire on social media, and is now raising awareness about the pitfalls of online marketplaces.

TikTok said they take the safety of their customers "extremely seriously" and that the product in question was removed from sale earlier this year, with the seller no longer active on TikTok shop.

Warning: This article contains graphic images and descriptions of injuries

Saffron, 27, said: "The fire suddenly exploded, engulfing me in flames. Within seconds, an ordinary evening turned into the most horrific experience of my life."

Saffron, from Cwmbran, Torfaen, was rushed to the bathroom by her partner and friends as her clothes melted off before her eyes. She remembered screaming "don't let me die" as her parents watched her skin and hair fall off.

The ambulance arrived shortly after, with a breathing tube saving her as her throat began to swell up.

"I went from being a happy, healthy young mum to fighting for my life in intensive care," she said.

Saffron also developed pneumonia and sepsis, and when doctors tried to wake her she developed severe intensive care delirium, which led to "horrific hallucinations that felt completely real".

"This was one of the most terrifying parts of my experience," she said.

"I genuinely believed nurses were setting me on fire and my partner had murdered our daughter."

For her family, it was like "living through a nightmare", with no certainty about whether she would wake up again.

At the end of August, Saffron woke up from her coma, but she did so with a body and life she "barely recognised".

"I had no voice, had tubes coming from everywhere and had to begin drinking through a syringe," she said.

"I kept waking up smelling fire and flashbacks of the accident."

Four months on and Saffron, from Cwmbran, said she is still recovering. The injuries to her hands have left her unable to work as a tattoo artist which she describes as a "huge part" of her identity.

"Losing that, alongside my independence and confidence, has been devastating," she added.

Her partner has become her full-time career, while also looking after their daughter, meaning they have an "incredibly uncertain future" navigating her recovery.

They have set up a GoFundMe for essential living costs and medical appointments to give their daughter the "stability she deserves".

"I'm incredibly lucky to be alive. Now I'm fighting to rebuild my health, my career and my family's future," Saffron said.

Saffron said she bought the table top fire as a "simple, affordable way" to create a nice atmosphere for her visitors.

She can "completely understand" why people would be attracted to these items as they look for affordable ways to heat their home.

"But I think it's important that people understand the potential risks before purchasing them," she added.

"I never bought mine believing I was putting myself or my family in danger."

Saffron tried to report the incident to TikTok, but the seller had shut down their page, meaning she was unable to file a complaint or report.

"I'm now facing multiple surgeries, ongoing rehabilitation, permanent scarring and an uncertain future with my career," she said.

"I'm not sharing my story for sympathy. I'm sharing it because I genuinely don't want another family to experience the pain, fear and heartbreak that mine has."

Sue Davies from Which? said it was "unacceptable" that people faced the risk of life-changing injuries from products bought from such a "well-known online marketplace".

"These sites claim that safety is a priority, but Which? investigations have exposed time and again their failure to prevent dangerous products from reaching UK consumers," she added.

She said the government had a "once in a generation opportunity" to make online shopping safer by ensuring the Product Regulation and Metrology Act makes online marketplaces legally responsible for the safety of products sold through their platforms, with tough penalties for those that break the rules.
