articles.title: Famed NFL agent reveals potential consequences for Steelers, Mike McCarthy after public Aaron Rodgers rupture
articles.summary: Famed agent Leigh Steinberg says Aaron Rodgers' public accusations against Steelers coach Mike McCarthy could deter future free agents from Pittsburgh.
articles.body: Famed NFL agent Leigh Steinberg says Aaron Rodgers’ public rupture with the Pittsburgh Steelers and his allegations against coach Mike McCarthy could prompt questions from agents advising potential players about joining the Steelers in the future, and tarnish Rodgers' lasting memory in the NFL. "This is about as far away from an ideal parting as can be imagined," Steinberg told OutKick. Steinberg, whose former clients include Steelers quarterbacks Ben Roethlisberger, Kordell Stewart and Neil O’Donnell, criticized Rodgers for taking the dispute public, saying the quarterback was undermining the kind of farewell most accomplished players hope to have. "But for Rodgers to have this long, illustrious career and then go out this way is certainly not ideal because his critique of the team, whether accurate or not, is exposing dirty laundry to the world," he said. Steinberg also suggested Rodgers understood exactly how much attention his comments would attract. "Pat McAfee didn’t have to do much interviewing," he said. "He just, he asked a couple questions and Aaron took it from there." "So he knew what he was doing." STEELERS COACH MIKE MCCARTHY INJURES HIMSELF AND IT WAS SERIOUS ENOUGH HE NEVER GOT TO HALFTIME LOCKER ROOM Rodgers accused McCarthy of falling asleep and snoring during meetings and missing team events during a Wednesday appearance on ESPN’s "The Pat McAfee Show." The interview followed Pittsburgh’s announcement that Rodgers would be inactive for Friday’s game against the Denver Broncos, with Mason Rudolph starting. NFL Network subsequently reported that Pittsburgh was waiving Rodgers. But Steinberg said the public nature of Rodgers’ accusations did not absolve Pittsburgh of examining them. "The Steelers have to look at themselves and ask, are any of these allegations true?" he said. "Is there dysfunction in the coaching ranks?" Steinberg stressed that he could not independently determine whether Rodgers’ account was accurate. "Only the people involved know," he said. The consequences could extend beyond Rodgers’ departure, according to Steinberg, who said the allegations would warrant questions from agents helping players evaluate Pittsburgh as a destination. Asked how he would advise a high-value client considering signing with the Steelers, he said he would seek answers directly from team leadership. "You would certainly have discussions with their front office as to whether or not these allegations are true," he said. Steinberg said Rodgers had described a distant, uninvolved coach, making it necessary for agents to establish the facts rather than simply accept either the quarterback’s account or the franchise’s reputation. SUPER BOWL CHAMPION JOE THEISMANN REVEALS KEY FACTOR IN AARON RODGERS DECISION TO RETURN TO STEELERS That would mean weighing the allegations against Pittsburgh’s history of stability, including its limited coaching turnover. "So you certainly want to understand the facts," he said. Steinberg’s own experience with the organization offered a favorable view of its leadership. Over years of representing Pittsburgh quarterbacks, he said, the front office consistently emphasized players’ interests and the franchise’s future. "Every discussion I ever had with their front office, they were looking to the long view. They cared about players," he said. He also praised owner Art Rooney II and general manager Omar Khan. "I’ve dealt many times with Omar Khan and many times with Art Rooney, and they’ve been nothing but classy." That history, Steinberg suggested, makes the current controversy particularly difficult for an organization that has long prided itself on its culture. "They’ve always had a reputation as the epitome of stability, class, a unique culture," he said. "When people put on the Steelers uniform, they tend to play better." Steinberg described the deterioration of Rodgers’ relationship with McCarthy, who previously coached him in Green Bay, as "stunning." For Steinberg, the issue was not simply that a quarterback and coach disagreed. It was that a dispute ordinarily handled inside a franchise had become a public spectacle. He said teams generally want to work through internal criticism while presenting unity to the outside world. Asked whether McCarthy should be held responsible for the situation, Steinberg declined to assign blame solely to the coach. "I don’t have the inside information," he said, adding that the stories Rodgers told were "disturbing stories for a franchise." "I’m sure they’ll take a look at the conduct and evaluate it." His broader assessment placed responsibility on the fractured relationship. "I think it’s a mutual breakdown," he said. Asked whether he had seen a comparable situation involving such a high-profile player publicly criticizing his coach, Steinberg answered, "No." "First of all, it’s shocking that Aaron Rodgers gets benched. articles.title: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un urges wider tactical nuclear deployment during inspection of weapons facilities
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country should focus on deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and that its nuclear material production capacity was being systematically expanded, state media KCNA reported on Thursday.
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un said his country should focus on deploying tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains and that its nuclear material production capacity was being systematically expanded, state media KCNA reported on Thursday. Kim, who spoke during an inspection of nuclear material production and weapons research facilities, also said North Korea’s status as a nuclear weapons state was “absolutely inviolable”. KCNA did not identify the facilities or their locations. “Our nuclear capability is now a reality,” KCNA quoted Kim as saying. North Korea’s status as a nuclear weapons state would not change because of outside assertions or what he called “denuclearization rhetoric from forces that ignored objective reality and failed to recognize the changed situation.” Kim said North Korea should “focus on utilizing tactical nuclear weapons across multiple domains for different missions” and called recent achievements in nuclear weapons production a major success in carrying out the country’s nuclear force policy. He also said any attempt to deny North Korea’s nuclear status, which it enshrined in its constitution in 2023, would be regarded as “an open declaration of war” and said Pyongyang would never relinquish what it called a core guarantee of national sovereignty and security. “Our possession of nuclear weapons is an absolutely irreversible choice as long as malicious forces exist that use nuclear weapons as a means of achieving hegemony,” Kim said. North Korea has conducted six nuclear tests since 2006, with its last and most powerful test carried out in 2017. South Korea’s defense minister said in August that Pyongyang was generally believed to possess between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads, but said the estimate came from private research organizations and could not be officially confirmed.

articles.title: Kushner calls Putin ‘grandmaster of politics’
articles.summary: U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, called Russian President Vladimir Putin a “grandmaster of politics” following U.S.-backed trilateral peace talks that have yielded little progress. “President Putin is very organized. You know, people can like what he’s done. They cannot like what he’s done. But he’s definitely a grandmaster of politics,” Kushner said…
articles.body:
U.S. special envoy Jared Kushner, President Trump’s son-in-law, called Russian President Vladimir Putin a “grandmaster of politics” following U.S.-backed trilateral peace talks that have yielded little progress.

“President Putin is very organized. You know, people can like what he’s done. They cannot like what he’s done. But he’s definitely a grandmaster of politics,” Kushner said during an interview on the “MD Meets” podcast .

He called Putin a “historic figure” who was always “very well prepared” when they met to discuss a possible end to Russia’s war with Ukraine. The conflict is nearing its fifth year, with American leaders pushing for its end.

“He takes a lot of notes when we’re speaking, and then he transmits very specifically, but it’s very clear he has a very deep understanding of the issues. He has some very strong perspectives on them,” Kushner continued.

The special envoy stated that in his opinion Putin didn’t only want peace but also wanted to use negotiations to “try and change the relationship with America” in order to create a “new beginning.”

Moscow and Kyiv held their first U.S.-mediated talks in nine months earlier this month in Abu Dhabi, during which they agreed to a “large-scale” exchange of prisoners of war.

Kushner also announced Russian leaders agreed to allow European partners to participate in peace negotiations after he visited Moscow. He continued that the Russians are open to accepting Ukraine maintaining robust security guarantees — meaning enforceable commitments designed to deter future aggression.

He stated he understood the “skepticism and disbelief” in Russia holding to that position but said it’s important to start dialogue between Europe and the Kremlin.

The war between the countries is still raging as Kyiv targeted Russia’s Kerch bridge for the third time in three days. The bridge connects Russia with the occupied Crimean Peninsula and works as a symbol of Putin’s commitment to hold on to the territory since Russia annexed it in 2014. The recent attacks damaged a portion of the bridge’s road.

Russia is escalating its attacks against Ukrainian energy infrastructure and civilian targets across the country. One recent attack hit the Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia, killing two people and wounding 48 others, according to The Associated Press , citing officials.

articles.standfirst: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.summary: Confira quando cai o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026 e a data limite para o pagamento do salário.
articles.body:
Quando será o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026. — Foto: Rafa Neddermeyer/Agência Brasil

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O último mês do ano está chegando e, junto a ele, o último pagamento. Para trabalhadores com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026 será sábado, 5 de dezembro. Para o cálculo do prazo de pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil, enquanto domingos e feriados não entram na contagem.

A regra está prevista no artigo 459 da Consolidação das Leis do Trabalho (CLT), que determina que o salário deve ser pago, no máximo, até o quinto dia útil do mês seguinte ao trabalhado.

Quando é o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026?

No cálculo do prazo para pagamento do salário, são considerados os dias de segunda-feira a sábado. Domingos e feriados ficam fora da contagem.

Primeiro dia útil : 1º de dezembro (terça-feira);

Segundo dia útil : 2 de dezembro (quarta-feira);

Terceiro dia útil : 3 de dezembro (quinta-feira);

Quarto dia útil : 4 de dezembro (sexta-feira);

Quinto dia útil : 5 de dezembro (sábado).

Portanto, para quem trabalha com carteira assinada, o quinto dia útil de dezembro de 2026 será no sábado (5).

Sábado conta como dia útil para o pagamento do salário?

Sim. Para a contagem do prazo previsto na CLT para o pagamento de salários, o sábado é considerado dia útil.

A contagem é interrompida aos domingos e feriados. Por isso, mesmo que o trabalhador não tenha expediente aos sábados, o dia entra no cálculo do quinto dia útil.

Essa regra é específica para o prazo de pagamento do salário e não significa que o sábado seja necessariamente um dia normal de trabalho para todos os empregados.

O que acontece se o salário não for pago até o quinto dia útil?

O artigo 459 da CLT estabelece o prazo máximo para o pagamento do salário. Se o empregador não cumprir a data-limite, o trabalhador pode buscar orientação para cobrar os valores atrasados.

Em caso de atraso, o empregado pode recorrer à Justiça do Trabalho para cobrar o pagamento devido, com os acréscimos que forem aplicáveis. O sindicato da categoria também pode auxiliar na defesa dos direitos dos trabalhadores e na adoção das medidas cabíveis.

Atrasos frequentes ou prolongados no pagamento podem caracterizar descumprimento das obrigações do empregador.

Dependendo das circunstâncias e da gravidade da situação, isso pode levar ao reconhecimento da rescisão indireta, quando o trabalhador encerra o contrato por falta grave do empregador e pode ter direito às verbas de uma demissão sem justa causa.

O empregador também pode estar sujeito à fiscalização e às penalidades previstas na legislação trabalhista.

articles.title: O que se sabe sobre os cães mortos após enxurrada em canil  | G1
articles.standfirst: Associação que atende mais de 200 animais em Descalvado (SP) também perdeu ração, medicamentos e vacinas após temporal que provocou alagamentos na cidade.
articles.summary: Associação que atende mais de 200 animais em Descalvado (SP) também perdeu ração, medicamentos e vacinas após temporal que provocou alagamentos na cidade.
articles.body:
Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

Três cães idosos e Vinicius, um animal paralítico, morreram após uma enxurrada atingir o canil da Associação Protetora dos Animais de Descalvado (SP) , a APAD, na madrugada de quarta-feira (25). Além das mortes, dois gatos ficaram em estado grave.

"Então ele não teve nenhuma chance. Era o nosso menino aqui do canil. A gente chegou a fazer cirurgia nele, ele fazia tratamento e a nossa esperança é que um dia ele fosse voltar a andar, mas infelizmente o Vinícius não teve esse final feliz", afirmou a administradora do canil, Rosa Cortapasso, ao falar sobre o cão paralítico.

A associação, que abriga mais de 200 animais, também perdeu alimentos, cobertores, casinhas, medicamentos, vacinas e equipamentos usados no atendimento veterinário. (Veja mais informações abaixo).

Cão Vinícius morreu afogado durante chuva em Descalvado (SP) — Foto: Renan Ciconelo/EPTV

Segundo a Defesa Civil, choveu cerca de 135 milímetros. A água invadiu uma das áreas mais baixas do abrigo, onde estavam animais debilitados que não conseguiram escapar da enxurrada.

Os animais foram levados para um hospital veterinário em uma universidade de Descalvado , onde passam por atendimento. A prioridade para os voluntários é recuperá-los e depois, aos poucos, reconstruir a ONG.

"A gente foi ligando, as pessoas vieram, então tem bastante gente da prefeitura aqui. Tem voluntários também que vieram, tem pessoas de outra ONG também que veio aqui para ajudar a gente. E toda ajuda é bem-vinda , quem puder também, mesmo que seja para carregar alguma coisa, ajudar, dar uma comida para os cachorros, remédio, alguma coisa, porque a gente está tudo perdido aqui ", disse a voluntária Natália Cortapasso.

Animais não conseguiram escapar da enxurrada

Cão Vinícius morreu afogado após enxurrada atingir canil em Descalvado (SP) — Foto: EPTV/Reprodução

A água invadiu a sala de cirurgia da associação, onde estavam animais que precisavam de cuidados especiais. Alguns deles tinham dificuldades de locomoção e não conseguiram sair a tempo.

Segundo a administradora da ONG, Rosa Cortapasso, três cães idosos e Vinícius, que era paralítico e passava por tratamento na entidade, morreram afogados.

A perda abalou quem acompanhava de perto a rotina do animal. A voluntária Natália Cortapasso contou que tinha o costume de tirar fotos com Vinícius todos os dias e que também costumava passear com ele.

Chuva causa estragos em ONG que cuida de mais de 200 animais em Descalvado (SP) — Foto: Renan Ciconelo/EPTV

A força da água também atingiu os espaços de armazenamento e provocou a perda de diversos materiais utilizados no dia a dia da associação.

Sacos de ração, cobertores, colchões, casinhas, vacinas e medicamentos foram atingidos pela enchente.

Parte dos remédios e das vacinas ficava armazenada em uma geladeira, mas os produtos acabaram espalhados pelo chão depois que a água invadiu o local.

De acordo com a voluntária, algumas vacinas chegaram a ser retiradas e colocadas no gelo na tentativa de preservar os produtos, mas ainda havia dúvidas sobre a possibilidade de aproveitamento, já que eles ficaram expostos à água e fora da refrigeração adequada.

Chuva causou estragos em ONG que cuida de mais de 200 animais em Descalvado (SP) — Foto: Renan Ciconelo/EPTV

Mesmo diante dos prejuízos e da perda dos animais, os voluntários começaram a limpeza ainda durante a manhã. A prioridade é recuperar a estrutura e garantir que os mais de 200 animais atendidos pela entidade continuem recebendo os cuidados necessários.

Com os prejuízos provocados pelo temporal, a APAD precisa da colaboração da população para recuperar os materiais perdidos e manter o atendimento aos animais.

A associação pede doações de ração, cobertores, medicamentos e outros itens necessários para a rotina dos animais.

Quem quiser ajudar pode procurar a entidade pelas redes sociais, no Instagram e no Facebook, pelo perfil @apad. descalvado .

Por esses canais, os interessados podem obter informações sobre os itens mais urgentes e as formas de contribuição.

articles.summary: Investimento médio de R$ 5 mil por aluno já qualificou quase seis mil pessoas para o setor entre 2025 e 2026, com novos editais previstos para o próximo ano.
articles.body:
Capacitações gratuitas oferecem certificações técnicas e treinamentos essenciais para o embarque profissional — Foto: Arquivo Secom

Adicione o g1 como Fonte Preferida no Google

O morador de Macaé Anderson Teixeira conquistou uma vaga no setor offshore após concluir os cursos gratuitos de T-HUET e delineador oferecidos pela Prefeitura. Mesmo sem experiência anterior na função, ele garantiu uma oportunidade em uma empresa local e, dois meses depois, já estava trabalhando embarcado.

Segundo Anderson, o conhecimento adquirido nas aulas foi determinante para ingressar no mercado de trabalho, além de representar uma economia significativa ao evitar gastos que comprometeriam o orçamento familiar.

Formações são definidas em alinhamento com as demandas de empresas do setor energético que atuam no município — Foto: Arquivo Secom

A trajetória do trabalhador integra as políticas públicas de qualificação profissional do município voltadas à cadeia produtiva de óleo e gás. De acordo com a Secretaria de Qualificação Profissional, quase 6 mil pessoas foram capacitadas entre 2025 e 2026 em áreas como operador de ROV (veículo operado remotamente em operações submarinas), salvatagem (CBSP), soldagem de aço carbono, pintura industrial, acesso por cordas e delineador.

No mercado atual, as certificações obrigatórias para o embarque offshore custam entre R$ 4 mil e R$ 5 mil ao trabalhador. Para viabilizar o acesso gratuito, a Prefeitura investiu, em média, R$ 5 mil por participante, atendendo tanto profissionais que buscavam apenas certificações de embarque quanto moradores que aprenderam uma nova profissão do zero.

A trilha formativa pode começar pelos treinamentos básicos de segurança, como CBSP e T-HUET, e avançar para especializações técnicas. A pasta ressaltou ainda que a grade de cursos é estruturada a partir de reuniões constantes com a Petrobras e empresas terceirizadas que atuam em Macaé, garantindo que a oferta acompanhe as demandas reais de contratação.

Além das formações voltadas ao setor offshore, o órgão informa ter capacitado mais de 10 mil moradores em cursos de outras áreas, como manicure e confeiteiro. A secretaria também mantém a plataforma Qualificados, ferramenta digital que conecta alunos e egressos a empresas parceiras para ampliar a inserção profissional.

articles.title: Expect fewer frosts and more hot days as UK seasons shift, says Met Office
articles.summary: Changing seasons are affecting wildlife and leading some farmers to grow different crops.
articles.body:
The UK's seasons are changing, with fewer winter frosts and more hot summer days, according to new analysis from the Met Office.

Across the UK, the number of winter days with an air frost – when the air temperature falls to 0C or below – was around a quarter lower in the decade to 2025 than during the period from 1961 to 1990.

In southern England, the reduction was around a third while the average number of UK summer days reaching 25C has more than doubled.

The Met Office says climate change has led to these seasonal shifts.

"Our summer is getting wider and our winter is getting smaller," says Dr James Pope, climate scientist at the Met Office.

"The driver of this is that the whole global climate is warming. And that impacts on the UK.

"Some areas went from their wettest ever winter to a severe drought via a record-breaking summer for the whole country."

The changing conditions have affected wildlife and led some farmers to grow different crops.

Some of the biggest reductions in winter air frosts have been in England, Wales and Northern Ireland, where the average number of days has fallen by around 11 compared with 1961 to 1990.

Southern England has seen other significant changes. In Cornwall, the average number of winter air frost days has almost halved, falling from around 18 to just 10.

On the Isle of Wight, the figure has also fallen by almost half, from around 21 to 11 days.

Scotland remains the frostiest UK nation, but has also seen a reduction, from around 45 to 38 winter air frost days.

Summer days reaching 25C have become more common across the UK.

Some of the biggest increases have been in southern England, where the average number of summer days reaching 25C has more than doubled, from just over eight to more than 16.

In Essex and Suffolk, they have risen by almost 13 days in both counties.

The Met Office defines a hot day as one where the temperature reaches 30C or above.

Across the UK, the average number of these days has increased fourfold, from 0.3 to 1.2 per summer.

The increase is particularly striking in Greater London, where days reaching 30C have risen from an average of 1.3 to 6.1 per summer.

Summer 2026 was the hottest on record , according to provisional Met Office data.

There were five widespread heatwaves and 40 days of temperatures above 30C, smashing the previous record of 34 days.

"Humans, animals and crops are encountering extremes of temperature that we've not seen before and this is a physiological challenge to all three," says Thomas Crocker, science manager with the Met Office's climate security team.

This has led to water challenges, he says, with wet winters causing problems with planting, pests and diseases.

Dry summers have meant there has not been enough water to grow crops.

"The impact on horticulture is seismic, it's affected all crops," says John Walgate, CEO of British Growers, which represents most British horticultural organisations growing vegetable and fruit.

Walgate says this year's weather has been particularly tough for brassicas like cauliflowers, cabbages and broccoli, with yields down by about 50%.

Irrigated crops such as onions, potatoes and carrots also suffered from a lack of water due to low rainfall and hot temperatures.

It's not all been bad though. Walgate says soft fruit such as strawberries have had a "good year".

Tim Young and his family have been farming in Norfolk since the 1960s.

But his arable crops - onions, wheat and sugar beet - have been struggling because of the hotter, drier summers and fewer cold days in winter which kill bugs.

With some crop yields decreasing, Young has been looking at ways to diversify the farm's income and planted a vineyard three years ago.

Last year he harvested double the expected amount of grapes.

"With climate change, the frontier is moving further north of where we can grow grapes," he says.

Despite annual variations in weather, he is confident it can be profitable.

Changing weather patterns are shifting where species live and when they migrate, breed and feed, says Zoe Quiroz Cullen, head of climate and international policy at The Wildlife Trusts charity.

Warmer winters mean bats are waking from hibernation when there are too few insects to feed, she says, while amphibians emerging and spawning earlier can be caught out by cold snaps.

Meanwhile, warmer springs mean oak trees are coming into leaf earlier than usual, and caterpillars are hatching earlier.

The UK's bird population has fallen in recent decades, largely because of habitat loss and climate change , external .

Starlings and swifts have declined significantly, although milder winters and conservation work have helped some species thrive.

Kevin Anderson, visitor experience officer at Somerset Wildlife Trust, has worked at Avalon Marshes for 15 years and has seen its bird life change first-hand.

Thirty to 40 years ago, he says, it would have been rare to see an egret north of the Mediterranean.

Now the reserve is home to a growing population of great white egrets taking advantage of warmer winters which allow them to fish all year round.

The birds first bred in Somerset in 2012, with just two nests. Last year, about 73 chicks were born in Avalon Marshes with the population thought to be around 200 now.

Climate change - mainly the result of the burning of fossil fuels - is raising average temperatures in the UK .

The current global warming level is 1.4C above pre-industrial levels, climate scientists estimate.

The Met Office says changes to the UK's seasons are expected to continue as temperatures rise.

If global warming reaches 2C above pre-industrial levels, the UK could experience an average of about 24 winter air frost days, compared with 38 during the period from 1961 to 1990.

The average number of days reaching 25C could rise to around 15 per summer, compared with just over four during the earlier period.

Crocker says the UK's weather in the coming years is going to vary.

"There's still going to be some cooler summers, there's still going to be some drier winters - but that baseline has shifted."

He says we will see more extreme hot weather and more record-breaking hot days, but we are less likely to experience extreme cold weather.

And Met Office research shows summer extending into autumn, and the possibility of less autumn rainfall in the future.

But Dr Pope says there will always be four distinct seasons in the UK.

The analysis has been done by the Met Office as it begins a new partnership with the BBC to provide weather data for weather forecasts, as well as additional insight and expertise on our changing climate.

articles.title: A meeting with Democrats over healthcare? Trump says he’s open to it
articles.summary: Experts tell Al Jazeera they are sceptical that Trump would back Medicare for All, a proposal for national healthcare.
articles.body:
Just weeks after attacking Abdul El-Sayed on the campaign trail, United States President Donald Trump says he will meet with the incoming Democratic senator to discuss Medicare for All, a proposal to establish a national healthcare programme.

Trump confirmed his willingness to sit down with El-Sayed in an interview with the New York Post on Tuesday, calling the Democrat a “smart guy”.

“I know I’ll be meeting with him,” Trump said. “Maybe there’s some place in the middle that we could go.”

A former public health official in Detroit, El-Sayed catapulted to national prominence in the 2026 midterm elections, when he won a hotly contested Senate seat in Michigan. A central part of his platform has been expanding access to healthcare.

In an interview with Zeteo this month, El-Sayed even floated renaming Medicare for All after Trump.

“If he wants to pass Trumpcare for All, I’m OK with it,” El-Sayed told host Mehdi Hasan. “He seems to like to put his name on things.”

Days later, he posted on social media a mockup of a gold-colored insurance card, bearing Trump’s signature and the name “Trumpcare”.

In an accompanying caption, El-Sayed asked the president to “guarantee health care for every American, from cradle to grave”.

The White House initially dismissed the proposal. Then, on Saturday, Trump shared El-Sayed’s image of the card on Truth Social. In his interview with the New York Post, Trump also called the “Trumpcare” branding “very smart”.

El-Sayed is pitching a government-run health insurance programme, which would cover “all necessary healthcare” and still allow private insurance.

Trump has not endorsed the proposal, and there is no set date for the meeting.

But with Democrats set to take control of the US Congress in January, healthcare advocates and political experts are closely watching what will come out of any potential meeting between the two politicians.

It remains unclear what Trump’s support could mean for the effort to get guaranteed healthcare for every American.

For more than a century, the US has weighed the possibility of offering universal healthcare access. But such proposals in recent decades have faced stiff opposition from the private sector.

During the Great Depression in the 1930s, for instance, President Franklin D Roosevelt appointed a Committee on Economic Security whose mission was to address the need for “all forms of social insurance”, including healthcare.

While a national health bill did not pass during Roosevelt’s administration, his successor, Harry Truman, became the first US president to propose a comprehensive national health insurance system in 1945. It failed amid fierce opposition from the American Medical Association, which called it “socialized medicine”.

Twenty years later, President Lyndon B Johnson signed two government insurance programmes, Medicare and Medicaid, into law. But their scope was limited to providing coverage for older Americans and some people in low-income brackets or with special needs.

Since then, a number of Democratic leaders have tried different paths to expand coverage.

In 1994, President Bill Clinton’s plan proposed giving everyone healthcare through private insurance, with employers required to help pay for it. Insurers ran advertisements warning the plan would limit people’s medical choices, and the plan died without a vote amid divisions in the US Congress.

The next Democratic president, Barack Obama, took up the fight to expand healthcare access again in the new millennium.

His name became associated with a sweeping overhaul of the US healthcare system — the Affordable Care Act, popularly known as “Obamacare” — that passed in 2010.

The Affordable Care Act expanded Medicaid, helped people pay for private insurance and made it illegal for insurers to turn people away because of pre-existing conditions. But a proposal to let people buy a government-run plan alongside private options failed in the US Senate.

During the 2016 and 2020 presidential campaigns, Senator Bernie Sanders, an independent who caucuses with Democrats, made Medicare for All a centrepiece of his platform, proposing a federal plan to replace most private insurance, including the coverage people get through work.

While the idea was embraced by progressives, Democrats as a whole were divided over whether to replace private coverage and who would bear the cost.

Sanders and his allies introduced another bill in 2025, but it has yet to pass through the US Congress.

Eagan Kemp, a healthcare policy expert at the consumer advocacy nonprofit Public Citizen, believes such proposals have struggled because of the economic heft the healthcare industry wields.

“I think the big reason is profit,” said Eagan Kemp. He described the country’s medical system as the “Wild West”.

In the 1980s, US healthcare costs were similar to those in other countries, according to Kemp.

But the American system became more corporatised and driven by profit, he explained, and it lacked the regulation many countries introduced as they moved towards universal healthcare.

Kemp argued that programmes like Medicare for All would rein in what companies can charge, how much care they can cut and how much profit they can take out of the system.

It would also cut out the insurance middlemen that drive up costs and make it harder for people to get the care they need, he said.

Experts note that Trump’s flirtation with El-Sayed’s Medicare for All proposal isn’t drawing the amount of opposition that would be expected for what has historically been a very partisan issue.

Republican strategist Ashley Davis, who worked in President George W Bush’s administration, told Al Jazeera she was bullish that Trump could pick up some bipartisan support on healthcare, an area she says he’s been “focused on”.

“I’m actually happy they’re meeting because, maybe for once, Republicans and Democrats can get along and something productive will come out of this,” Davis told Al Jazeera.

However, she expressed doubt that a bill resembling Medicare for All will materialise from any meeting with El-Sayed, saying agreements to lower drug prices , provide more funds for rural healthcare or expand Medicare for children are much more likely.

In order to pass something like Medicare for All, Davis explained that “you would have to bring on some of the new [Democratic] senators in really red states”.

“It sounds great from a talking point perspective, but how it actually gets accomplished is a whole other thing,” she added.

Kemp was also sceptical that a policy like Medicare for All could cruise through the US Congress to Trump’s desk, citing the high number of political donations that lawmakers receive from healthcare and insurance providers.

“How much they’d be willing to do, or how quickly they’d be willing to move, is yet to be determined,” he said of the country’s Congress members. “I’m sceptical that there would be votes there.”

But Kemp noted that Trump has a tendency to break from Republican orthodoxy. The fact that he is not competing on the ballot in 2028 could also help pave the way for healthcare discussions with Democrats.

It may also be the last chance for Trump, who has described himself as a world-class dealmaker, to get a major piece of legislation passed during his final two years in the White House, according to Kemp.

“If it was any other Republican president in my lifetime, I wouldn’t hold much hope,” he said. “But I think this one will be interesting to see play out.”

articles.title: A typical new home in the US now sells for $393,300, almost $40,000 less than an existing home, the widest gap on record, as 43% of builders cut prices last month to lure more buyers
articles.summary: If you were shopping for a home in the US right now, would you buy a new-build property or an older house?
articles.body: If you were shopping for a home in the US right now, would you buy a new-build property or an older house? Your answer carries significant weight now because buying a newly built home is much cheaper than buying an existing one. While housing remains largely unaffordable, the latest data from the National Association of Home Builders (NAHB)/Wells Fargo Cost of Housing Index (CHI) show that a typical new home now costs almost $40,000 less than an existing home in the third quarter of 2026. The gap is the widest since the CHI began tracking it.Builders are slashing prices and offering incentives to attract buyersIt may not be surprising that builders are becoming increasingly aggressive in their efforts to attract buyers. Prospective homebuyers may find builders particularly willing to negotiate, as weaker demand pushes more developers to cut prices and offer incentives. According to NAHB Chairman Bill Owens, 43 per cent of builders cut prices in October, the highest share since 2020, and 65 per cent offered sales incentives.“New-home affordability improved slightly in the third quarter while existing-home affordability held steady, giving new homes their widest affordability advantage since the CHI began,” Bill Owens, also a homebuilder and remodeler from Worthington, Ohio, said in a release.NAHB Chief Economist Robert Dietz also agreed that, while builders are working to make new homes affordable, housing costs continue to strain household budgets.“Builders are working with buyers to make new homes more affordable and appealing in a tough market, yet the latest CHI data show housing costs still overburden families. As builders contend with rising construction costs, tighter lending standards and persistent labour shortages, policymakers should remove regulatory obstacles, enact permitting reform and create a stronger business environment that enables builders to produce more attainable, affordable homes,” Dietz said.Prices for new homes fell, but the cost of existing homes remains higherThe median new home sold for $393,300, down 4.2 per cent from $410,700 in the second quarter. The median existing home sold for $432,900, down only 0.5 per cent from $434,900, according to the data. Most of the widening came from new-home prices dropping, while resale prices barely moved.What does this shift mean for a typical family? A family earning the national median income of $106,800 needed 33 per cent of its income to cover the mortgage on a median-priced new home, down from 34 per cent in the second quarter. The same family would need 36 per cent of its income for an existing home.The index assumes a 10 per cent deposit and includes taxes, insurance and mortgage insurance. The average 30-year mortgage rate used in the calculations rose from 6.51 per cent in the second quarter to 6.79 per cent in the third.5 most cost-burdened marketsAccording to the latest data, San Jose-Sunnyvale-Santa Clara, California, was the most cost-burdened market, with 79 per cent of median income needed for an existing-home mortgage. The other four were:Urban Honolulu, Hawaii (73%)San Diego-Chula Vista-Carlsbad, California (70%)San Francisco-Oakland-Fremont, California (66%)Barnstable Town, Massachusetts (61%)Of the 175 markets NAHB studied, eight were severely cost-burdened, meaning families spend more than half their income on housing.5 least cost-burdened marketsDecatur, Illinois, was the least cost-burdened market, at 17 per cent on the CHI. Other markets include:Elmira, New York (18%)Peoria, Illinois (19%)Wichita Falls, Texas (20%)Springfield, Illinois (20%)Davenport-Moline-Rock Island, Iowa-Illinois (20%)Low-income households in these markets would need to set aside between 34 and 41 per cent of their earnings for mortgage payments on a median-priced existing home.While the price cuts and incentives are helping, Owens says policymakers need to do more. “Policymakers must do more to reduce red tape, address labour shortages and fix supply chains so builders can expand the nation’s housing supply.”For prospective buyers, the data suggest that new homes are more affordable relative to existing homes than at any point in the index's history. However, monthly mortgage payments would still account for a substantial share of most families' incomes.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? Build Your Legacy with TOI Homes.

articles.title: France's political mainstream risks presidential vote debacle with no clear candidate
articles.summary: Hard-right and hard-left candidates dominate the polls ahead of next year's presidential election.
articles.body:
France's political mainstream faces wipe-out at the presidential election in April-May 2027, unless it acts fast to choose who it wishes to stand.

With every poll confirming the dominance of hard-right and hard-left leaders Marine Le Pen and Jean-Luc Mélenchon, candidates of the middle-ground – the old "legacy" parties – are being squeezed out of the game.

In theory any contender from centre-right or centre-left who was chosen in the first multi-candidate round of voting in April should be in a strong position to win in the play-off a fortnight later.

That is because at their separate ends of the spectrum both Le Pen and Mélenchon have more people who oppose than support them.

But personal rivalries, lack of preparation and differing political visions have so far put paid to any hope of a meaningful challenge.

"The game in the centre is totally blocked," says political writer François Fressoz at the left-leaning Le Monde newspaper. "The partisans of reason have lost their reason."

On the left – the old Socialist Party and its acolytes – there is at least agreement on a candidate: European Parliament MP Raphaël Glucksmann.

His problem is that allies who he might once have counted on – Greens, Communists and other small left-wing parties, not to mention many Socialist voters – are being pulled inexorably into the Mélenchon orbit.

In the last two weeks, Green party leader Marine Tondelier, a majority of Communist parliamentary deputies and one-time Socialist presidential hopeful Benoît Hamon have all thrown in their lot with the leader of France Unbowed (LFI).

Another prominent figure of the left – François Ruffin – has also withdrawn from the race, bowing to the unbowed Mélenchon's now almost total command of the field.

So with the soft-left emasculated, the main hope for an alternative to Le Pen and Mélenchon has to be focused on the right. But here the prospects – which until recently seemed bright – are now clouded with gloom.

"A Mélenchon–Le Pen duel in round two is not yet inevitable," says Guillaume Tabard, political analyst at the conservative Le Figaro newspaper. "But it is looking increasingly probable."

In recent weeks the poll ratings of the main centre-right hopeful Edouard Philippe – a former prime minister under President Macron – have fallen sharply, and he is now consistently placed behind Mélenchon in the first round of the vote. Marine Le Pen is way ahead of both.

Other candidates for command of this centre-right "space" are circling. They include another former Macron prime minister, Gabriel Attal; the leader of the right-wing Republicans (and former Macron interior minister), Bruno Retailleau; and now – a surprise new challenger – the mayor of Cannes, David Lisnard.

Lisnard, who stands on a liberal economic platform of less state and lower taxes, has emerged from nowhere to become the man of the hour. Membership of his micro-party Nouvelle Energie (New Energy) has shot up to more than 100,000, and he is being taken seriously as a possible Philippe replacement.

But this very multiplicity of names – not to mention others like judoka Teddy Riner, journalist Natacha Polony and former prime minister Dominique de Villepin – betrays the essential weakness of the centre-right challenge.

According to veteran commentator Nicolas Baverez, "If you want to win an election, it's quite simple: you need a strategy, a programme, and activists. Right now in the space between Le Pen and Mélenchon we have none of that: there is a total vacuum.

"The most glaring absence is digital. Mélenchon especially, but Le Pen too, are running extremely effective social media campaigns. In the middle… nothing."

Guillaume Tabard agrees that the lack of a shared platform is proving a serious handicap.

"In recent weeks we have seen Marine Le Pen issue her manifesto proposals for reforming pensions. We have seen Jean-Luc Mélenchon publish his programme in a best-selling book," he says.

"What do we have in between? Arguments about names and polling figures and whether or not there should be a primary. It's not, to put it mildly, an encouraging start."

For Fressoz, "There is no-one in the centre who is taking up the fight. When Le Pen makes her proposals about pensions, there is no-one saying, 'Hang on, that doesn't add up!'. Macron – who did after all take her on and beat her – is said to be furious."

Any mention of Macron, though, is most unwelcome for the camp that nominally is his heir. Philippe, Attal and Retailleau all served under a president who Baverez now calls "as toxic as Trump", so deep is his unpopularity in the country. Lisnard, by contrast, makes much of his refusal to serve under Macron – but he faces another handicap.

According to Fressoz, "Lisnard has shot up in the polls because he is on the right of the right, and there is always an appetite for a figure who is not Le Pen, but who speaks her kind of language on immigration.

"But Lisnard is an economic liberal, and in France that is a minority taste. He'll have his moment but then he will deflate."

With five months to go to until the election, all is not lost for the mainstream. Optimists in its ranks say that come the new year, opinion polls will start settling behind one or other centre-right candidate, and the others will feel obliged to step aside.

Talk of a centre-right primary – as occurred ahead of the 2017 election – is beginning to ebb. The two strongest candidates, Philippe and Lisnard, are opposed. Lisnard says he supports one but his conditions are designed to be unacceptable to the rest. Retailleau and Attal are in favour – but that, says Tabard, is "mainly as a way to keep their hopes alive."

In theory then it is possible a name will emerge in January or February, and start pulling behind him (or less likely, her) the mass of voters who do not want a disruptive radical as France's next head of state.

For Fressoz of Le Monde, "After years of Macron's 'neither left nor right', the left and right are once again shaping French politics. But now it is the extremes who are in control."

Le Pen and Mélenchon have both already run three times for the presidency. Their visions were defined long ago, their strategies laid, their activists trained. Polarisation is their friend, so is the social tension of recent weeks, and both are undisputed masters in their own camps.

The 2027 dénouement has been in their sights for years. That is their massive advantage.

articles.title: EU ‘strongly rejects’ rationale behind Trump’s tariffs
articles.summary: The European Union on Wednesday pushed back against the Trump administration’s allegations that the bloc’s industrial policies are contributing to a global oversupply of manufactured goods, after the U.S. proposed imposing 15 percent tariffs on imports from its 27 member countries. The European Commission rejected the findings of a months-long investigation by the Office of…
articles.body:
The European Union on Wednesday pushed back against the Trump administration’s allegations that the bloc’s industrial policies are contributing to a global oversupply of manufactured goods, after the U.S. proposed imposing 15 percent tariffs on imports from its 27 member countries.

The European Commission rejected the findings of a months-long investigation by the Office of the U.S. Trade Representative, which determined that the EU and 13 other trading partners engaged in practices that unfairly disadvantage American manufacturers.

“We will study the findings. At the same time we strongly reject the premise that Europe is a source of structural overcapacity. To the contrary, Europe is among those most exposed to overcapacity,” the commission’s deputy chief spokesperson Olof Gill said in a statement to Politico EU.

“The EU and the U.S. share a real concern about global overcapacity, much of it state-driven and concentrated in third countries. We regret the lack of joint action,” he added.

The Trump administration unveiled the proposed tariffs following an investigation launched in March under Section 301 of the Trade Act of 1974. The probe accused the EU of using extensive export financing to bolster production and exports.

U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer argued Wednesday that foreign industrial policies have undermined domestic manufacturing jobs for decades.

“For decades, many of our trading partners have adopted industrial strategies built on targeting manufacturing, wage and labor suppression, financial and other support, non-market economy inputs, and other market distorting practices that tilt the trade balance in their favor while eroding America’s manufacturing base,” Greer said in a statement.

The proposed 15 percent levy is consistent with the tariff ceiling negotiated by President Trump and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen as part of a trade agreement reached in July 2025.

Bernd Lange, chair of the European Parliament’s trade committee, called the administration’s findings “absurd” and accused Trump of circumventing the Supreme Court’s ruling earlier this year striking down his sweeping emergency tariffs.

“Neither the Supreme Court ruling nor the verdict of the voters has swayed Donald Trump. When a court strikes down the legal basis for his tariffs, he looks for another,” Lange said in a statement to Politico EU. “His aim remains the same. He uses tariffs to put pressure on trading partners and wring ever more concessions out of them.”

articles.title: In 2024, a Florida accounting clerk allegedly lost her job while recovering from cancer surgery and seeking temporary work restrictions; two years later, her employer agrees to pay her $112,500
articles.summary: Returning to work after cancer surgery can involve temporary physical limitations, but a Florida employee's request for a short period of workplace
articles.body: Returning to work after cancer surgery can involve temporary physical limitations, but a Florida employee's request for a short period of workplace adjustments allegedly cost her job. An accounting clerk recovering from cancer-related surgery was dismissed after asking her employer to accommodate restrictions on lifting, bending and squatting for three weeks, according to a federal discrimination lawsuit. Two years later, her former employer, Schumacher Auto Group, has agreed to pay her $112,500 and introduce changes to its workplace policies to settle the case.According to the US Equal Employment Opportunity Commission (EEOC), which announced the settlement on November 5, 2026, the Palm Beach County-based automotive dealership company agreed to resolve allegations that it violated the Americans with Disabilities Act (ADA). The settlement includes financial compensation for the former employee, disability accommodation policies, employee training and additional reporting requirements.Why the accounting clerk requested temporary work restrictionsThe dispute began in May 2024, when the accounting clerk was on leave recovering from cancer-related surgery. As she prepared to return to work, she requested reasonable accommodations to address her temporary physical limitations. According to the EEOC's lawsuit, her requested adjustments included a five-pound lifting restriction and avoiding repetitive squatting, bending or lifting for three weeks. These restrictions were intended to allow her to resume her employment while recovering from the surgery.However, instead of accommodating the request, Schumacher Auto Group terminated her employment, the agency alleged. The EEOC alleged that the company had failed to consider reasonable workplace adjustments that could have allowed the employee to return to her position. The agency also raised concerns about the employer's approach to employees returning from medical leave with physical restrictions. EEOC Miami District Director Evangeline Hawthorne described the case as an example of the harm caused by a blanket requirement that employees must be completely healed before returning to work.She explained that employers are required to consider individual circumstances and assess whether reasonable accommodations would allow an employee to perform the job.What the Americans with Disabilities Act requiresThe case centred on the Americans with Disabilities Act, a federal law that protects qualified employees with disabilities against workplace discrimination. Under the ADA, employers must provide reasonable accommodations for known disabilities unless doing so would cause undue hardship to their operations. Such adjustments can include modified work arrangements, changes to workplace practices or temporary restrictions that help employees perform their duties.The law also prohibits employers from discriminating against workers because of their disabilities, including terminating them on that basis. In this case, the EEOC alleged that Schumacher failed to accommodate the accounting clerk's medical restrictions and dismissed her after she requested adjustments. The agency maintained that the requested three-week restrictions should have been considered through the reasonable accommodation process.The EEOC first attempted to resolve the allegations through its administrative conciliation process. After those efforts, it filed a federal lawsuit against Schumacher Auto Group in the US District Court for the Southern District of Florida. The case was registered as EEOC v. Schumacher Auto Group, Inc., Case No. 9:26-cv-81322-EA.What the $112,500 settlement requiresUnder a four-year consent decree, Schumacher Auto Group will pay $112,500 in compensatory damages to the former accounting clerk. The agreement also requires the company to introduce a comprehensive disability accommodation policy. In addition to the financial payment, the dealership must provide regular training to its managers and employees on disability discrimination and their responsibilities under federal accommodation laws. It must also report complaints and accommodation requests to the EEOC during the decree's term.The settlement addresses both the employee's compensation and the company's future handling of disability-related workplace requests. EEOC Miami Regional Attorney Kristen Foslid said the agency appreciated Schumacher's willingness to resolve the matter at an early stage and its commitment to policy changes and training. She also emphasised that employers must understand their legal responsibilities when providing reasonable accommodations to employees with disabilities.The agreement brings the federal lawsuit to a resolution without a trial determining whether the alleged discrimination occurred. However, its requirements place specific obligations on Schumacher for the next four years. articles.title: Two Syrian security personnel killed in ISIL suicide attack
articles.summary: Syrian forces say the attack in northeastern Syria’s city of Hasakah involved four assailants who were all killed.
articles.body:
A suicide attack by the ISIL (ISIS) group has killed two security personnel and wounded five others in Syria’s northeastern city of Hasakah, according to local authorities.

Four gunmen targeted an Internal Security Forces (ISF) checkpoint on Wednesday in the Mushirfa neighbourhood of Hasakah, an official statement from the governorate’s media directorate said.

All four of the assailants died in the attack, two in clashes with security forces and the other two in suicide explosions, the ISF said.

One of the suicide attackers, Syrian media reported, was riding a booby-trapped motorcycle when he detonated himself at the entrance of the post.

The deputy governor of Hasakah, Ahmed al-Hilali, vowed “to uncover the circumstances of the attack and identify the perpetrators”.

“Ensuring the safety of citizens and the stability of the region is a responsibility from which we will not waver,” al-Hilali added.

The ISF shared photos from the site on their X page, including an image of the vest they say was worn by one of the two perpetrators who was “neutralised” by the forces.

A report in February by the UN said that Syrian President Ahmed al-Sharaa and two of his senior cabinet ministers were the targets of five foiled assassination attempts by ISIL over the past year.

The report did not provide specific dates as to when the foiled attacks took place, though it noted their locations in northern Aleppo, the country’s most populous province, and the southern province of Deraa.

In October, the Interior Ministry reported that two members of Syria’s internal security forces were killed and five wounded in clashes with a suspected ISIL cell during a raid on the outskirts of Damascus.

articles.body: Six family members from Florida were killed Tuesday when the small plane they were aboard crashed off the Mississippi coast on their way home from a fishing trip, according to reports. Those killed were identified by Jackson County Coroner Bruce Lynd Jr. as Brent Stokes, 50; Hunter Stokes, 16; Michael Knox, 43; Arlyn Knox, 43; Charles Holden Knox, 12; and Truett Knox, 10. COAST GUARD SUSPENDS SEARCH FOR BOSTON-BOUND MEDEVAC PLANE OFF NANTUCKET WITH 6 ON BOARD The plane lost contact with air traffic control at about 3:45 p.m., according to authorities. Divers from the Mississippi Department of Marine Resources located the remains of all six people inside the fuselage after an hours-long search, the U.S. Coast Guard said. articles.title: Photos: Storms and an El Nino-charged king tide batter California’s coast
articles.summary: Meteorologists have warned that the king tide could pair with high surf to bring historic surges to parts of the state.
articles.body:
California and other parts of the United States West Coast have experienced record-high water levels, causing flooding, destruction and dangerous waves.

On Wednesday, the National Oceanic and Atmospheric Administration (NOAA) announced that the fishing community of Charleston, Oregon, notched its highest-ever coastal water level, roughly 1.12 metres above the mean high water level.

It was as high as 3.4 metres above the mean low water mark.

Other NOAA stations recorded some of their highest water levels on record, including San Diego, Los Angeles and Santa Barbara, all on the southern California coast.

Further north, the L-shaped municipal pier in Pacifica, a city south of San Francisco, crumbled into the surf after a wave as tall as its platform crashed into it.

In a video on social media, bystanders could be heard voicing astonishment at the sight. “Oh my god, it’s gone. Oh my god,” one person said.

The pier had faced multiple closures in recent years, as seawater weakened its concrete structure, but experts say this week’s conditions were more dangerous than normal.

The high coastal water levels were spurred by a combination of factors, including a phenomenon popularly known as king tides.

The term is applied to the highest tides of the year, created when both the sun and the moon are aligned to create a larger-than-normal tidal bulge, pulling the water with their combined gravitational force.

The king tides have been exacerbated by the El Nino weather pattern as well as human-fuelled climate change.

While El Nino is a regular occurrence, this year’s edition is projected to be stronger than normal, according to forecasters, leading to record-warm waters off the Pacific coast. That warming, in turn, helps churn up powerful storms that contribute to waves battering the shoreline.

San Francisco Mayor Daniel Lurie announced on Wednesday that his city had made it through the worst of this week’s surge with flooding and waves up to 9 metres, but he warned of more king tides to come.

“The last two weeks have been an important reminder to get prepared for the rest of El Nino season. We’re expecting more king tides in December and January,” he wrote on social media. “We need to take these events seriously, prepare ahead of future storms, and stay alert.”

articles.title: Kim Jong Un says North Korea should widen deployment of tactical nukes
articles.summary: North Korean leader warns attempts to deny country’s nuclear status will be seen as “an open declaration of war”.
articles.body:
North Korean leader Kim Jong Un has urged his country to focus on deploying tactical nuclear weapons “across multiple domains for different missions”.

Kim said North Korea’s nuclear material production capacity was being systematically expanded on Thursday, according to state media KCNA.

Maintaining North Korea’s status as a nuclear-weapons state was “absolutely inviolable”, Kim said during an inspection of nuclear material production and weapons research facilities. KCNA did not identify the facilities or their locations.

The country’s status would not change because of what he called “denuclearisation rhetoric from forces that ignore objective reality and failed to recognise the changed situation”.

“Our nuclear capability is now a reality,” he said, calling recent achievements in nuclear weapons production a major success in carrying ⁠⁠out the country’s nuclear policy.

Any attempt to deny North Korea’s nuclear status, which it enshrined in its constitution in 2023, would be regarded as “an open declaration of war”, he said.

Kim said diversified use of tactical nuclear weapons was an “important and urgent task raised from tactical nukes’ military value in modern warfare and from the inevitable reality facing the border with the most dangerous enemy state”.

Kim’s statements come during a growing border dispute with South Korea over a landmine explosion that injured three South Korean soldiers in the Demilitarized Zone (DMZ), a heavily fortified territory between the two countries, on September 21.

Seoul demanded an apology from Pyongyang in October after a joint South Korea-United Nations investigation found that North Korea had planted the landmines more than a year ago.

Pyongyang sent a letter to the UN Security Council in response, accusing Seoul of fabricating the explosion, and fired about 10 short-range ballistic missiles off its east coast into the Sea of Japan less than a week later.

South Korea estimates that North Korea possesses between 80 and 120 nuclear warheads.

articles.title: MP woman loses husband in SUV crash involving police bus, DGP contests Rs 48 lakh compensation; high court raises it to Rs 60 lakh and orders DGP pay Rs 60,000 litigation cost to victims
articles.summary: BHOPAL: In a rare instance, the MP high court on Tuesday imposed a litigation cost of Rs 60,000 on the state director general of police (DGP) for opposing
articles.body: BHOPAL: In a rare instance, the MP high court on Tuesday imposed a litigation cost of Rs 60,000 on the state director general of police (DGP) for opposing the "higher" compensation awarded to persons killed and injured in a collision of an SUV with a police bus by the motor accident claims tribunal. The amount of litigation cost is for the claimants in the case.Six separate petitions were filed by the state govt through the DGP opposing the quantum of compensation awarded by the motor accident claims tribunal to victims of the accident while two petitions were filed by the victims and their families seeking higher compensation.The high court rejected the petitions presented on behalf of the DGP while partially allowing the petition of two claimants.The judge further imposed a litigation cost of Rs 10,000 in each case on the DGP for all the six appeals filed on his behalf in the high court and said the state govt will bear the cost. The case pertains to a collision of a police bus with an SUV in Seoni district on April 5, 2024, in which three persons travelling in the SUV were killed and two were injured.Cops can't dictate victims' treatment choices: MPHCOne of the major grounds taken by the DGP to oppose the "higher" amount of compensation was "contributory negligence" of both drivers in the collision. Dismissing the argument, the judge, Justice Vivek Agarwal, in his decision made public on Tuesday held that the point of "contributory negligence" could not be proved by the police and said "negligence on the part of the DGP or his officers is apparent in the investigation on face of record in not examining any independent witness to prove the factum of contributory negligence. Even the driver of the offending police bus has not been examined by the DGP."The court also dismissed the second ground that claimants Deepti Jaswani and Ashok Kukreja were given advantage by the tribunal on account of a permanent disability certificate.Terming the ground "funny", Justice Agarwal wrote it amounted to the police department pleading "with an iron fist" that claimants would not be free to choose treatment but would be restricted by "the whims and fancies of the police".The DGP had contended that treatment at district hospital, Mandla, would have cost far less than at Nagpur, which they preferred.The court raised compensation for Deepti Jaswani, whose husband, 45, was killed, from Rs 48 lakh to Rs 60 lakh, based on his annual income. articles.title: Netanyahu declares corruption trial has 'fallen apart' after judges question key charges
articles.summary: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu declared his corruption trial "fell apart" as judges urged prosecutors to rethink the bribery and fraud cases.
articles.body: The decade-long legal battle against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu suffered a major blow Wednesday after judges cast doubt on key corruption charges, prompting the Israeli leader to declare that his trial had "fallen apart" and demand an immediate end to the proceedings. A three-judge panel at the Jerusalem District Court suggested that Attorney General Gali Baharav-Miara consider dropping the most serious case against Netanyahu, questioned whether a criminal offense occurred in a second case and recommended resolving a third through a plea deal. "Today, the trial fell apart," Netanyahu said in an evening address following the proceedings, according to The Times of Israel. FROM INTELLIGENCE SHARING TO MISSILE DEFENSE, HOW ISRAEL'S PARTNERSHIP PROTECTS AMERICAN SECURITY "Ten years ago, I said, ‘There will be nothing because there was nothing.’ But it took 10 years for this truth to be revealed to everyone," he said. "Citizens of Israel, this trial must end immediately. And what also needs to end immediately is what came out of it — the hatred, the incitement, the division." The court's intervention dealt a major setback to prosecutors more than six years after Netanyahu's trial began and roughly a decade after authorities launched the initial probe into him. Judges had summoned Baharav-Miara to court Wednesday amid concerns over the strength of the prosecution's evidence and whether continuing the cases served the public interest. "We’re now at a crossroad and need to rechart a new path," Judge Rivka Friedman-Feldman told the attorney general, according to The New York Sun. "Public interest dictates a need to rethink." NETANYAHU REVEALS HE WANTS AMERICAN FINANCIAL SUPPORT FOR ISRAEL TO 'DRAW DOWN TO ZERO' She and her colleagues, Judges Moshe Bar-Am and Oded Shaham, stressed that their comments were preliminary, did not constitute a verdict and applied only to Netanyahu because they still had to hear the other defendants’ testimony, The Jerusalem Post reported. Baharav-Miara signaled that prosecutors would review the judges' recommendations and weigh their options. Netanyahu faces charges of bribery, fraud and breach of trust stemming from three corruption investigations. Prosecutors announced the charges in November 2019 and formally filed the indictment in January 2020, and Netanyahu consistently denied wrongdoing. The most serious charge, Case 4000, centers on allegations that Netanyahu granted regulatory favors to Israeli telecommunications giant Bezeq in exchange for favorable coverage on the Walla news website, which was then controlled by businessman Shaul Elovitch. Judges questioned whether prosecutors presented sufficient evidence to secure a conviction. In Case 2000, prosecutors also allege Netanyahu negotiated for favorable coverage from Yedioth Ahronoth newspaper publisher Arnon Mozes in exchange for legislation to weaken rival newspaper Israel Hayom. TRUMP WANTS LARGEST-EVER ISRAELI HEAVY BOMB TRANSFER — BUT PROPOSAL HAS CONGRESS PREPARING FOR $2.8B FIGHT The proposed deal never materialized, and judges questioned whether a criminal offense had happened. Case 1000 centers on allegations that Netanyahu and his wife, Sara, received almost $300,000 in gifts from Hollywood producer Arnon Milchan and Australian billionaire James Packer. Judges suggested resolving that case through an agreement. Zion Amir, an attorney who previously represented Netanyahu in the proceedings, rejected the prospect of a settlement. In his address Wednesday, Netanyahu also accused investigators of pressuring his political associates to testify against him and described the toll the investigations had taken on his family. "Ten years of terrible suffering for me, my wife and my sons," he said. "Of delusional interrogations. Of character assassination. Of grave incitement that wounds the soul. Who will give us back those 10 years?" Netanyahu, who requested a presidential pardon in November 2025 without admitting guilt, also called on his political opponents to set aside their differences and form a unity government. "The boycotts must end, and now," Netanyahu said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I know what enormous and immediate dangers the State of Israel faces. articles.title: FedEx cargo jet overshoots runway at Miami International Airport and stops just short of busy road
articles.summary: The Federal Aviation Administration issued a ground stop at Miami International Airport after a FedEx cargo jet overran the runway, causing Thanksgiving flight delays.
articles.body: The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) issued a ground stop at Miami International Airport Wednesday evening due to a disabled FedEx aircraft after it overshot the runway, disrupting flights amid the busy Thanksgiving holiday travel rush. Video from the scene shows a large FedEx cargo jet sitting near a fence that runs next to a busy road. The airport confirmed the aircraft overran Runway 26R, prompting all runways to close except for Runway 9R. Miami-Dade Fire Rescue responded to the airport and reported no injuries. The incident comes nearly three months after a Prime Air cargo jet overran Runway 30 at Miami International Airport, killing five people. FAA ISSUES GROUND DELAY AT CHICAGO O'HARE DUE TO 'EQUIPMENT OUTAGE' In a statement provided to Fox News Digital shortly before 10 p.m., the FAA said flights would be "resuming shortly" at the airport. The FAA said FedEx Flight 910, a McDonnell Douglas MD-11 arriving from Frederick W. Smith International Airport in Memphis, Tennessee, ran off the runway after landing in Miami. No injuries have been reported, according to the agency. The FAA is investigating the incident. FedEx confirmed the incident in a statement to Fox News Digital, saying the plane's crew was safe. "FedEx Flight 910 from Memphis to Miami experienced an issue upon landing Wednesday evening at Miami International Airport," a spokesperson said. "We are grateful that our crew is safe and there are no reported injuries." FedEx added that it was coordinating with investigators. According to an advisory issued by the FAA's Air Traffic Control System Command Center, the ground stop took effect at 8:16 p.m. In its advisory, the FAA said a disabled aircraft caused the ground stop and indicated a medium probability that the restrictions could be extended. The FAA said the pause was scheduled to remain in place until 9:45 p.m. WORST AIRPORTS FOR THANKSGIVING TRAVEL CHAOS RANKED AS MAJOR US HUBS TOP LIST According to an updated FAA advisory, Miami International Airport was experiencing average delays of 47 minutes, with maximum delays reaching two hours on Wednesday evening. articles.title: ‘Could be something good’: NCP (SP) leader Supriya Sule strikes softer tone on delimitation Bill
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying it would be premature
articles.body: NEW DELHI: NCP (SP) national working president Supriya Sule struck a softer tone on the Centre's proposed delimitation Bill, saying it would be premature to oppose the legislation before its details are known.Her comments come amid broader opposition resistance to the NDA government's push for delimitation."Let the bill come. Perhaps there could be something good in the Delimitation Bill," she told news agency PTI."Whether a bill is in the country's interest or not, opposing it just because you are in the opposition, or blindly supporting it because you are in power, is wrong for a healthy democracy. It is not necessary to oppose everything. We can also suggest improvements and say what changes should be made. There could be something good in it," Sule said.The NCP (SP) leader added that her party would discuss the legislation once it was introduced and support it if it served the country's interests.Her remarks on the Bill come at a time of heightened speculation over the possibility of Sharad Pawar's Nationalist Congress Party faction moving closer to the BJP-led NDA, triggering political chatter about a possible realignment in Maharashtra.Sule, however, sought to brush aside speculation about her party joining the ruling alliance or her getting a ministerial berth at the Centre or the Maharashtra chief minister's post, dismissing the claims as "gossip".Speaking to reporters in Karad on Wednesday, she said such speculation had followed her for years."For the last 12 years, I have been taking an oath as a minister. Don’t do this injustice to me. Since 2014, I have been made a minister," Sule told reporters.Sule rules out merger speculation after Ajit Pawar's deathMeanwhile, speculation about a possible merger between the two NCP factions led by Sharad Pawar and his nephew Ajit Pawar has also resurfaced.Sule had earlier said that the possibility of a merger had ended with the death of her cousin Ajit Pawar in an air crash. articles.title: FedEx plane overshoots Miami runway, causing temporary ground stop at airport
articles.summary: The brief ground stop comes on the day before the US Thanksgiving holiday, one of the busiest travel days of the year.
articles.body:
The Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has halted flights bound for Miami International Airport in Florida after a FedEx aircraft overran a runway on Wednesday evening.

Departures heading to Miami were grounded just after 20:15 local time (01:15 GMT) and all but one runway at the airport was closed, according to the FAA advisory. Flights are expected to resume by around 22:00 local time, the FAA told the BBC.

The airliner that ran past the runway arrived from Memphis. No injuries have been reported. The FAA is investigating the incident.

The ground stop comes on the day before Thanksgiving, one of the busiest travel days of the year in the US.

Flight delays in Miami reached one hour but appeared to be declining later Wednesday night.

Passengers scheduled to travel on Wednesday night were encouraged to check directly with their airlines for the latest flight updates before heading to the airport.

"We appreciate our passengers' patience as we work to safely resume normal operations," Miami-Dade Aviation Department spokesman Greg Chin said in a statement to the BBC.

The airport is among the top five domestic destinations for travelers in the country over this holiday week, according to the American Automobile Association.

The Miami-Dade area is under a flood watch until late Wednesday night. Periods of heavy rain throughout the day are expected to cause flooding, according to the US National Weather Service.

A nationwide ground stop earlier this month halted flights across the US for hours - the longest such event since the terror attacks on 11 September 2001.
